title.zh: 卷三百六十一 列傳第一百二十 張浚
title.raw: 卷三百六十一 列傳第一百二十 張浚 Volume 361 Biographies 120: Zhang Jun

sentences.zh: 張浚子:枃

translations.literal: Sons of Zhang Jun: Bing
translations.idiomatic: Sons of Zhang Jun: Bing

sentences.zh: 張浚，字德遠，漢州綿竹人，唐宰相九齡弟九皋之後。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun, courtesy name Deyuan, was a native of Mianzhu in Han Prefecture, a descendant of Tang Chancellor Zhang Jiuling's younger brother Zhang Jiugao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun, whose courtesy name was Deyuan, came from Mianzhu in Han Prefecture and was descended from Zhang Jiugao, younger brother of the Tang chancellor Zhang Jiuling.

sentences.zh: 父咸，舉進士、賢良兩科。

translations.literal: His father Xian passed the jinshi and xianliang examinations.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian had passed both the jinshi and xianliang examinations.

sentences.zh: 浚四歲而孤，行直視端，無誑言，識者知為大器。

translations.literal: Jun was orphaned at four. His conduct was upright and his gaze steady; he spoke no falsehoods. Those who knew him recognized him as a man of great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Jun lost his father when he was four. Upright in bearing and steady in gaze, he never spoke falsely, and those who knew him saw in him a man of great promise.

sentences.zh: 入太學，中進士第。

translations.literal: He entered the Imperial University and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Imperial University and obtained his jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 靖康初，為太常簿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingkang era, he served as clerk of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Jingkang era he served as a clerk in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 張邦昌僭立，逃入太學中。

translations.literal: When Zhang Bangchang usurped the throne, Jun fled into the Imperial University.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bangchang seized the throne unlawfully, Jun took refuge within the Imperial University.

sentences.zh: 聞高宗即位，馳赴南京，除樞密院編修官，改虞部郎，擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: On hearing that Gaozong had ascended the throne, he hurried to Nanjing. He was appointed Compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Public Works, and further promoted to Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Emperor Gaozong had taken the throne, he hastened to Nanjing. He was made a compiler at the Bureau of Military Affairs, then transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Public Works, and finally promoted to Palace Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 駕幸東南，後軍統制韓世忠所部逼逐諫臣墜水死，浚奏奪世忠觀察使，上下始知有國法。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage traveled southeast, troops under Rear Army Commander Han Shizhong chased a remonstrating official until he fell into the water and died. Jun memorialized stripping Han of his Observer commission, and from above to below people first came to know there was national law.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage moved into the southeast, men under Rear Army Commander Han Shizhong pursued a remonstrating official until he fell into the water and drowned. Jun memorialized that Han be stripped of his Observer commission, and for the first time court and camp alike understood that the law of the state held force.

sentences.zh: 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the post of Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 時乘輿在揚州，浚言：「中原天下之根本，願下詔葺東京、關陝、襄鄧以待巡幸。」

translations.literal: At that time the imperial carriage was at Yangzhou. Jun said: "The Central Plain is the root of all under Heaven. I beg Your Majesty to issue an edict to repair the Eastern Capital, Guan-Shaan, and Xiang-Deng to await an imperial tour."
translations.idiomatic: While the imperial carriage was at Yangzhou, Jun submitted: "The Central Plain is the foundation of the realm. I beg Your Majesty to decree the restoration of the Eastern Capital, Guan-Shaan, and Xiang-Deng, that they may await Your Majesty's progress."

sentences.zh: 咈宰相意，除集英殿修撰、知興元府。

translations.literal: This offended the chief ministers' wishes; he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Assembling Excellence and given concurrent appointment as prefect of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: His words ran counter to the chief ministers' intent, and he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Assembling Excellence with concurrent charge as prefect of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 未行，擢禮部侍郎，高宗召諭曰：「卿知無不言，言無不盡，朕將有為，正如欲一飛沖天而無羽翼，卿勉留輔朕。」

translations.literal: Before he departed, he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites. Gaozong summoned him and instructed: "You know how to speak without holding back and to speak fully without reserve. I intend to act—I am just like one who wishes to soar to the heavens but has no wings. Do your utmost to remain and assist me."
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites. Gaozong summoned him and said: "You speak without reserve and to the full. I mean to act, yet I am like one who would soar to the heavens but lacks wings. Do your utmost to stay and assist me."

sentences.zh: 除禦營使司參贊軍事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Counselor on Military Affairs in the Imperial Guard Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Counselor on Military Affairs in the Imperial Guard Commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 浚度金人必來攻，而廟堂晏然，殊不為備，力言之宰相，黃潛善、汪伯彥皆笑其過計。

translations.literal: Jun judged that the Jurchens would certainly come to attack, yet the court was at ease and made no preparations at all. He pressed this on the chief ministers; Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan both laughed at him for overcalculating.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was convinced the Jurchens would attack, yet the court sat at ease and made no preparations. He pressed the matter on the chief ministers Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan, who both laughed at him for alarmism.

sentences.zh: 建炎三年春，金人南侵，車駕幸錢塘，留朱勝非于吳門捍禦，以浚同節制軍馬，已而勝非召，浚獨留。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year of Jianyan, the Jurchens invaded south. The imperial carriage went to Qiantang. Zhu Shengfei was left at Wu Gate to defend; Jun was given joint command of the army. Soon Shengfei was recalled and Jun alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year of Jianyan the Jurchens invaded south. The imperial carriage went to Qiantang. Zhu Shengfei was left at Wu Gate to hold the defense, and Jun was given joint command of the armies. Soon Shengfei was recalled, and Jun alone remained.

sentences.zh: 時潰兵數萬，所至剽掠，浚招集甫定。

translations.literal: At the time tens of thousands of scattered troops plundered wherever they went; Jun gathered and pacified them only gradually.
translations.idiomatic: At that time tens of thousands of scattered soldiers plundered wherever they passed; Jun gathered and settled them only with difficulty.

sentences.zh: 會苗傅、劉正彥作亂，改元赦書至平江，浚命守臣湯東野秘不宣。

translations.literal: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rebelled, the amnesty proclamation for the change of reign reached Pingjiang. Jun ordered the defending official Tang Dongye to keep it secret and not promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: When Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan rose in rebellion, the amnesty proclamation for the change of reign reached Pingjiang. Jun ordered the defending official Tang Dongye to keep it secret and not announce it.

sentences.zh: 未幾，傅等以檄來，浚慟哭，召東野及提點刑獄趙哲謀起兵討賊。

translations.literal: Before long Fu and the others sent their manifesto. Jun wept bitterly and summoned Dongye and Judicial Intendant Zhao Zhe to plan raising troops to punish the traitors.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Fu and his party sent their manifesto. Jun wept bitterly and summoned Dongye and Judicial Intendant Zhao Zhe to plan raising troops to punish the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時傅等以承宣使張俊為秦鳳路總管，俊將萬人還，將卸兵而西。

translations.literal: At that time Fu and the others had appointed Commissioner Zhang Jun commander of Qinfeng Circuit. The general was leading ten thousand men back and was about to disband his troops and go west.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fu and his party had appointed Commissioner Zhang Jun commander of Qinfeng Circuit. The general was bringing ten thousand men back and was about to disband his force and march west.

sentences.zh: 浚知上遇俊厚，而俊純實可謀大事，急邀俊，握手語故，相持而泣，因告以將起兵問罪。

translations.literal: Jun knew the emperor favored the general deeply, and that he was honest and could be enlisted for a great enterprise. He urgently invited him, took his hands and spoke of old times, held each other weeping, and told him they would raise troops to call them to account.
translations.idiomatic: Jun knew the emperor held the general in high favor and that he was honest and fit to be enlisted for a great undertaking. He urgently invited him, clasped his hands and spoke of old times, and they held each other weeping as Jun told him they would raise troops to call the rebels to account.

sentences.zh: 時呂頤浩節制建業，劉光世領兵鎮江，浚遣人齎蠟書，約頤浩、光世以兵來會，而命俊分兵扼吳江。

translations.literal: At that time Lü Yihao was directing Jianye and Liu Guangshi held the army at Zhenjiang. Jun sent men bearing sealed letters to summon Yihao and Guangshi to bring troops to join, and ordered the general to divide his forces to hold Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lü Yihao was directing affairs at Jianye and Liu Guangshi commanded the army at Zhenjiang. Jun sent men bearing sealed letters to summon Yihao and Guangshi to bring their troops to join him, and ordered the general to divide his force and hold Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 上疏請復辟。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial requesting restoration of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial requesting that the emperor be restored to the throne.

sentences.zh: 傅等謀除浚禮部尚書，命將所部詣行在，浚以大兵未集，未欲誦言討賊，乃托雲張俊驟回，人情震讋，不可不少留以撫其軍。

translations.literal: Fu and the others planned to appoint Jun Minister of Rites and order him to lead his troops to the temporary court. Jun, since the great army had not yet assembled and he did not wish to proclaim openly that he was punishing the traitors, pleaded that the general had suddenly returned, the people were shaken with fear, and he could not but stay a little longer to calm the army.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and his party planned to appoint Jun Minister of Rites and order him to lead his troops to the temporary court. Because the great army had not yet assembled and he did not wish to proclaim openly that he was punishing the rebels, Jun pleaded that the general had suddenly returned, the people were shaken with fear, and he could not but remain a little longer to steady the army.

sentences.zh: 會韓世忠舟師抵常熟，張俊曰：「世忠來，事濟矣。」

translations.literal: When Han Shizhao's fleet reached Changshu, the general Zhang Jun said: "With Shizhao come, the affair will succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When Han Shizhao's fleet reached Changshu, General Zhang Jun said: "Now that Shizhao has come, the affair will succeed."

sentences.zh: 白浚以書招之。

translations.literal: He told Jun and had a letter sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: He informed Jun and had a letter sent to summon Shizhao.

sentences.zh: 世忠至，對浚慟器曰：「世忠與俊請以身任之。」

translations.literal: When Shizhao arrived, he said to Jun weeping: "Shizhao and the general beg to bear this in our own persons."
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhao arrived, he said to Jun through tears: "Shizhao and the general beg to bear this upon ourselves."

sentences.zh: 浚因大犒俊、世忠將士，呼諸將校至前，抗聲問曰：「今日之舉，孰順孰逆？」

translations.literal: Jun thereupon feasted the officers and men of the general and Shizhao generously, called all commanders before him, and asked in a ringing voice: "Of today's undertaking, which is obedient and which is rebellious?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun thereupon feasted the officers and men under the general and Shizhao on a grand scale, called all commanders before him, and asked in a ringing voice: "Of today's undertaking, which side is loyal and which rebellious?"

sentences.zh: 眾皆曰：「賊逆我順。」

translations.literal: All said: "The traitors are rebellious; we are obedient."
translations.idiomatic: All answered: "The rebels are in the wrong; we are in the right."

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「聞賊以重賞購吾首，若浚此舉違天悖人，汝等可取浚頭去；

translations.literal: Jun said: "I hear the traitors offer heavy rewards for my head. If this undertaking of mine violates Heaven and betrays men, you may take my head;
translations.idiomatic: Jun said: "I hear the rebels offer a heavy reward for my head. If this undertaking of mine violates Heaven and betrays men, you may take my head;

sentences.zh: 不然，一有退縮，悉以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: otherwise, whoever retreats will be dealt with by military law."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, whoever retreats will be punished by military law."

sentences.zh: 眾感憾憤。

translations.literal: The crowd was moved and stirred to anger.
translations.idiomatic: The troops were moved and burned with indignation.

sentences.zh: 於是，令世忠以兵赴闕，而戒其急趨秀州，據糧道以俟大軍之至。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Shizhao to lead troops to the capital, and warned him to hurry to Xiuzhou, hold the grain route, and await the arrival of the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he ordered Shizhao to lead his troops toward the capital, and warned him to hurry to Xiuzhou, hold the grain route, and await the arrival of the main force.

sentences.zh: 世忠至秀，即大治戰具。

translations.literal: When Shizhao reached Xiuzhou, he immediately set to preparing war equipment on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhao reached Xiuzhou, he at once began large-scale preparations of war equipment.

sentences.zh: 會傅等以書招浚，浚報云：「自古言涉不順，謂之指斥乘輿；

translations.literal: When Fu and the others sent letters to recruit Jun, Jun replied: "From antiquity speech that is disrespectful to the sovereign is called railing at the imperial carriage;
translations.idiomatic: When Fu and his party sent letters to win Jun over, Jun replied: "From antiquity, words that are disrespectful to the sovereign are called railing at the imperial carriage;

sentences.zh: 事涉不遜，謂之震驚宮闕；

translations.literal: acts that lack deference are called shaking the palace;
translations.idiomatic: acts that lack deference are called disturbing the palace;

sentences.zh: 廢立之事，謂之大逆不道，大逆不道者族。

translations.literal: deposing and establishing—that is called great treason; great traitors are punished with execution of the whole clan.
translations.idiomatic: deposing and establishing the ruler—that is called great treason, and great traitors are punished with the extermination of their clans.

sentences.zh: 今建炎皇帝不聞失德，一旦遜位，豈所宜聞。」

translations.literal: Now the Jianyan Emperor has heard of no loss of virtue, yet in a single day he has been made to abdicate—this should never be heard of."
translations.idiomatic: Now the Jianyan Emperor has been heard of no loss of virtue, yet in a single day he has been made to abdicate—such a thing should never be heard of."

sentences.zh: 傅等得書恐，乃遣重兵扼臨平，亟除俊、世忠節度使，而誣浚欲危社稷，責柳州安置。

translations.literal: When Fu and the others received the letter they were afraid. They sent a heavy force to hold Linping, hastily appointed the general and Shizhao military commissioners, and slandered Jun as wishing to endanger the state, ordering him exiled to Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu and his party received the letter they were afraid. They sent a heavy force to hold Linping, hastily appointed the general and Shizhao as military commissioners, and slandered Jun as wishing to endanger the state, ordering him exiled to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 俊、世忠拒不受。

translations.literal: The general and Shizhao refused to accept.
translations.idiomatic: The general and Shizhao refused to accept the appointments.

sentences.zh: 會呂頤浩、劉光世兵踵至，浚乃聲傅、正彥罪，傳檄中外，率諸軍繼進。

translations.literal: When Lü Yihao and Liu Guangshi's armies arrived in succession, Jun proclaimed the crimes of Fu and Zhengyan, issued proclamations within and without, and led the armies forward in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When the armies of Lü Yihao and Liu Guangshi arrived in succession, Jun proclaimed the crimes of Fu and Zhengyan, issued proclamations throughout the realm, and led the armies forward in turn.

sentences.zh: 初，浚遣客馮轓以計策往說傅等，會大軍且至，傅、正彥憂恐不知所出。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jun had sent his guest Feng Fan with stratagems to persuade Fu and the others. When the great army was about to arrive, Fu and Zhengyan were anxious and did not know what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had sent his client Feng Fan with stratagems to persuade Fu and his party. When the great army was about to arrive, Fu and Zhengyan were anxious and at a loss.

sentences.zh: 轓知其可動，即以大義白宰相朱勝非，使率百官請復辟。

translations.literal: Fan knew they could be moved, and immediately expounded the great principle to Chief Minister Zhu Shengfei, having him lead the hundred officials to request restoration of the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Fan knew they could be swayed and at once set forth the great principle to Chief Minister Zhu Shengfei, urging him to lead the hundred officials in requesting restoration of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 高宗御筆除浚知樞密院事。

translations.literal: The emperor in his own hand appointed Jun Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in his own hand appointed Jun Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 浚進次臨平，賊兵拒不得前，世忠等搏戰，大破之，傅、正彥脫遁。

translations.literal: Jun advanced to Linping. The rebel army blocked him and he could not advance. Shizhao and the others fought fiercely and routed them badly; Fu and Zhengyan fled in escape.
translations.idiomatic: Jun advanced and halted at Linping. The rebel army blocked his path and he could not advance. Shizhao and the others fought fiercely and routed them; Fu and Zhengyan slipped away in flight.

sentences.zh: 浚與頤浩等入見，伏地涕泣待罪，高宗問勞再三，曰：「曩在睿聖，兩宮隔絕。

translations.literal: Jun entered with Yihao and the others to have audience. They prostrated themselves weeping and awaiting punishment. Gaozong inquired after and comforted them repeatedly, saying: "Formerly at Rui Palace the two palaces were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Jun entered with Yihao and the others to have audience. They prostrated themselves weeping and awaiting punishment. Gaozong inquired after them and comforted them again and again, saying: "Formerly at Rui Palace the two palaces were cut off from each other.

sentences.zh: 一日啜羹，小黃門忽傳太母之命，不得已貶卿郴州。

translations.literal: One day while sipping soup, a young eunuch suddenly conveyed the Grand Empress Dowager's command—I had no choice but to demote you to Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: One day as I was sipping soup, a young eunuch suddenly conveyed the Grand Empress Dowager's command, and I had no choice but to demote you to Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 朕不覺羹覆於手，念卿被謫，此事誰任。」

translations.literal: I did not notice the soup spill in my hand. Thinking of your exile—who bore the blame for this?"
translations.idiomatic: I did not even notice the soup spill in my hand. When I think of your exile—who bore the blame for this?"

sentences.zh: 留浚，引入內殿，曰：「皇太后知卿忠義，欲識卿面，適垂簾，見卿過庭矣。」

translations.literal: He kept Jun, led him into the inner hall, and said: "The Grand Empress Dowager knows your loyalty and righteousness and wished to see your face. She has just now been behind the curtain and saw you pass the courtyard."
translations.idiomatic: He kept Jun and led him into the inner hall, saying: "The Grand Empress Dowager knows your loyalty and wished to see your face. She has just now been behind the curtain and saw you pass through the courtyard."

sentences.zh: 解所服玉帶以賜。

translations.literal: He removed the jade belt he wore and bestowed it on him.
translations.idiomatic: He removed the jade belt he was wearing and bestowed it on him.

sentences.zh: 高宗欲相浚，浚以晚進，不敢當。

translations.literal: Gaozong wished to make Jun chief minister; Jun, being a latecomer, did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong wished to make Jun chief minister, but Jun, as a man of recent advancement, did not dare accept.

sentences.zh: 傅、正彥走閩中，浚命世忠追縛之以獻，與其黨皆伏誅。

translations.literal: Fu and Zhengyan fled to Fujian. Jun ordered Shizhao to pursue and bind them for presentation; they and their partisans were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: Fu and Zhengyan fled into Fujian. Jun ordered Shizhao to pursue and bind them for presentation; they and their partisans were all executed.

sentences.zh: 初，浚次秀州，嘗夜坐，警備甚嚴，忽有客至前，出一紙懷中曰：「此苗傅、劉正彥募賊公賞格也。」

translations.literal: Earlier when Jun was at Xiuzhou, one night he sat up with very strict guard. Suddenly a visitor came before him, took out a paper from his robe and said: "This is the reward placard of Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan for recruiting assassins against you."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Jun was stationed at Xiuzhou, he once sat up at night under very strict guard. Suddenly a visitor came before him, drew a paper from his robe, and said: "This is the reward placard of Miao Fu and Liu Zhengyan for hiring assassins against you."

sentences.zh: 浚問欲何如，客曰：「僕河北人，粗讀書，知逆順，豈以身為賊用？

translations.literal: Jun asked what he wished to do. The visitor said: "I am a man of Hebei, have read a little, know rebellious from obedient—how could I let my person be used by traitors?
translations.idiomatic: Jun asked what he intended. The visitor said: "I am a man of Hebei and have read a little. I know the difference between rebellion and loyalty—how could I let my person be used by traitors?

sentences.zh: 特見為備不嚴，恐有後來者耳。」

translations.literal: I only saw your precautions were not strict and feared there might be those who came after me."
translations.idiomatic: I only saw that your precautions were not strict and feared there might be others who came after me."

sentences.zh: 浚下執其手，問姓名，不告而去。

translations.literal: Jun came down and took his hand, asked his name; he would not tell and left.
translations.idiomatic: Jun came down and took his hand, asking his name, but the man would not tell him and departed.

sentences.zh: 浚翌日斬死囚徇于眾，曰：「此苗、劉刺客也。」

translations.literal: Next day Jun executed a condemned prisoner and displayed him to the crowd, saying: "This was Miao and Liu's assassin."
translations.idiomatic: The next day Jun executed a condemned prisoner and displayed him to the crowd, saying: "This was the assassin sent by Miao and Liu."

sentences.zh: 私識其狀貌物色之，終不遇。

translations.literal: Privately he marked his appearance but never met him again.
translations.idiomatic: Privately he memorized the man's appearance and sought him out, but never encountered him again.

sentences.zh: 巨盜薛慶嘯聚淮甸，至數萬人。

translations.literal: The great bandit Xue Qing gathered and roared in the Huai region, reaching tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: The great bandit Xue Qing gathered his forces and roared across the Huai region, reaching tens of thousands of men.

sentences.zh: 浚恐其滋蔓，徑至高郵，入慶壘，喻以朝廷恩意。

translations.literal: Jun feared he would spread further and went straight to Gaoyou, entered Qing's camp, and expounded the court's gracious intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jun feared he would spread further, went straight to Gaoyou, entered Qing's camp, and expounded the court's gracious intent.

sentences.zh: 慶感服下拜，浚留撫其眾。

translations.literal: Qing was moved and knelt in submission; Jun remained to pacify his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Qing was moved and knelt in submission; Jun remained to pacify his followers.

sentences.zh: 或傳浚為賊所執，呂頤浩等遽罷浚樞筦。

translations.literal: Someone reported that Jun had been seized by bandits; Lü Yihao and the others hastily dismissed Jun from the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Someone reported that Jun had been seized by bandits, and Lü Yihao and the others hastily removed him from the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 浚歸，高宗驚歎，即日趣就職。

translations.literal: When Jun returned, Gaozong exclaimed in amazement and that same day urged him to resume office.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun returned, Gaozong exclaimed in amazement and that same day urged him to resume his post.

sentences.zh: 浚謂中興當自關陝始，慮金人或先入陝取蜀，則東南不可保，遂慷慨請行。

translations.literal: Jun said that restoration must begin in Guan-Shaan, fearing the Jurchens might first enter Shaan to take Shu—then the southeast could not be preserved—and so asked leave to go forth in fervor.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held that restoration must begin in Guan-Shaan, fearing that if the Jurchens first entered Shaan and seized Shu the southeast could not be preserved, and so he asked leave to go forth with fervor.

sentences.zh: 詔以浚為川、陝宣撫處置使，得便宜黜陟。

translations.literal: He was appointed Pacification and Disposition Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi, with authority to promote and demote as expedient.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him Pacification and Disposition Commissioner for Sichuan and Shaanxi, with authority to promote and demote officials as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 將行，禦營平寇將軍范瓊，擁眾自豫章至行在。

translations.literal: As he was about to depart, Imperial Guard Pacification General Fan Qiong led a crowd from Yuzhang to the temporary court.
translations.idiomatic: As he was about to depart, Imperial Guard Pacification General Fan Qiong led a large force from Yuzhang to the temporary court.

sentences.zh: 先是，靖康城破，金人逼脅君、後、太子、宗室北行，多瓊之謀；

translations.literal: Earlier when the Jingkang city fell, the Jurchens coerced the ruler, empress, crown prince, and imperial clansmen to go north—much of this was Qiong's counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Jingkang capital fell, the Jurchens coerced the ruler, empress, crown prince, and imperial clansmen to go north—much of this was Qiong's doing;

sentences.zh: 又乘勢剽掠，左右張邦昌，為之從衛。

translations.literal: again he took advantage to plunder, attended Zhang Bangchang, and served as his escort guard.
translations.idiomatic: again he took advantage of the turmoil to plunder, attended Zhang Bangchang, and served as his escort.

sentences.zh: 至是入朝，悖傲無禮，且乞貸逆党傅、正彥等死罪。

translations.literal: Now he came to court arrogant and without courtesy, and moreover begged to spare the traitorous partisans Fu, Zhengyan and others from capital punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Now he came to court insolent and without courtesy, and moreover begged that the traitorous partisans Fu, Zhengyan, and others be spared from capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 浚奏瓊大逆不道，乞伸典憲。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized that Qiong was guilty of great treason and begged to apply the statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized that Qiong was guilty of great treason and begged that the statutes be applied.

sentences.zh: 翌日，召瓊至都堂，數其罪切責之，送棘寺論死。

translations.literal: Next day he summoned Qiong to the Hall of Administration, enumerated his crimes and rebuked him severely, and sent him to the prison office for death sentence.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he summoned Qiong to the Hall of Administration, enumerated his crimes and rebuked him sharply, and sent him to the prison office for sentencing to death.

sentences.zh: 分其軍隸神武軍，然後行。

translations.literal: He divided Qiong's army and attached it to the Divine Martial Army, then departed.
translations.idiomatic: He divided Qiong's army and attached it to the Divine Martial Army, and only then set out.

sentences.zh: 與沿江襄、漢守臣議儲蓄，以待臨幸。

translations.literal: With defending officials along the Yangtze and in Xiang-Han he discussed storing provisions to await the imperial visit.
translations.idiomatic: With the defending officials along the Yangtze and in Xiang-Han he discussed storing provisions to await the imperial visit.

sentences.zh: 高宗問浚大計，浚請身任陝、蜀之事，置幕府于秦川，別遣大臣與韓世忠鎮淮東，令呂頤浩扈蹕來武昌，復以張俊、劉光世與秦川相首尾。

translations.literal: Gaozong asked Jun his grand plan. Jun asked to bear Sichuan-Shaan personally, establish a headquarters at Qinchuan, separately send a great minister with Han Shizhao to guard Huai East, have Lü Yihao escort the sovereign to Wuchang, and again use General Zhang Jun, Liu Guangshi with Qinchuan as head and tail.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong asked Jun his grand strategy. Jun asked to bear Sichuan and Shaanxi himself, establish a headquarters at Qinchuan, send a great minister separately with Han Shizhao to guard Huai East, have Lü Yihao escort the imperial progress to Wuchang, and again coordinate General Zhang Jun and Liu Guangshi with Qinchuan as head and tail.

sentences.zh: 議既定，浚行，未及武昌，而頤浩變初議。

translations.literal: When the plan was settled Jun departed. Before reaching Wuchang, Yihao changed the initial plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the plan was settled Jun set out. Before he reached Wuchang, Yihao altered the original plan.

sentences.zh: 浚既抵興元，金人已取鄜延，驍將婁宿孛堇引大兵渡渭，攻永興，諸將莫肯相援。

translations.literal: After Jun reached Xingyuan, the Jurchens had already taken Yan'an. The fierce general Lou Sicheng led a great army across the Wei and attacked Yongxing; none of the generals would aid each other.
translations.idiomatic: After Jun reached Xingyuan, the Jurchens had already taken Yan'an. The fierce general Lou Sicheng led a great army across the Wei to attack Yongxing, and none of the generals would aid one another.

sentences.zh: 浚至，即出行關陝，訪問風俗，罷斥奸贓，以搜攬豪傑為先務，諸將惕息聽命。

translations.literal: When Jun arrived he immediately went out through Guan-Shaan, inquired into customs, dismissed corrupt officials, and made gathering heroes his first task; the generals trembled and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun arrived he at once went out through Guan-Shaan, inquired into local customs, dismissed corrupt officials, and made gathering heroes his first task; the generals trembled and obeyed his orders.

sentences.zh: 會諜報金人將攻東南，浚命諸將整軍向敵。

translations.literal: When scouts reported the Jurchens would attack the southeast, Jun ordered the generals to array the army against the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When scouts reported that the Jurchens would attack the southeast, Jun ordered the generals to array their armies against the enemy.

sentences.zh: 已而金人大攻江、淮，浚即治軍入衛。

translations.literal: Soon the Jurchens launched a major attack on the Yangtze and Huai; Jun immediately led the army in to guard the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Jurchens launched a major attack on the Yangtze and Huai regions, and Jun immediately led his army in to guard the capital region.

sentences.zh: 至房州，知金人北歸，復還關陝。

translations.literal: Reaching Fang Prefecture, he learned the Jurchens had returned north and went back to Guan-Shaan.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Fang Prefecture he learned the Jurchens had returned north and went back to Guan-Shaan.

sentences.zh: 時金帥兀術猶在淮西，浚懼其復擾東南，謀牽制之，遂決策治兵，合五路之師以復永興。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin commander Wuzhu was still in west Huai; Jun feared he would again trouble the southeast and planned to tie him down, and so decided to drill troops and unite the armies of five circuits to recover Yongxing.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jin commander Wuzhu was still in western Huai. Jun feared he would again trouble the southeast and planned to tie him down, and so decided to drill troops and unite the armies of five circuits to recover Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 金人大恐，急調兀術等由京西入援，大戰于富平。

translations.literal: The Jurchens were greatly alarmed and urgently shifted Wuzhu and others through Jingxi to reinforce; a great battle was fought at Fu Ping.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens were greatly alarmed and urgently shifted Wuzhu and others through Jingxi to reinforce; a great battle was fought at Fu Ping.

sentences.zh: 涇原帥劉錡身率將士薄敵陳，殺獲頗眾。

translations.literal: Jingyuan commander Liu Qi personally led his officers and men to press the enemy line and killed and captured quite many.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingyuan commander Liu Qi personally led his officers and men to press the enemy line and killed and captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 會環慶帥趙哲擅離所部，哲軍將校望見塵起，驚遁，諸軍皆潰。

translations.literal: But Huanqing commander Zhao Zhe left his post without authorization; Zhe's officers saw dust rise and fled in panic, and all armies collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: But the Huanqing commander Zhao Zhe left his post without authorization. Zhe's officers and men saw dust rise in the distance and fled in panic, and all the armies collapsed.

sentences.zh: 浚斬哲以徇，退保興州。

translations.literal: Jun executed Zhe to warn the others and retreated to defend Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun executed Zhe as a warning to the others and retreated to defend Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 命吳玠聚兵扼險於鳳翔之和尚原、大散關，以斷敵來路，關師古等聚熙河兵於岷州大潭，孫渥、賈世方等聚涇原、鳳翔兵于階、成、鳳三州，以固蜀口。

translations.literal: He ordered Wu Jie to gather troops to hold the dangerous passes at Monk's Plain near Fengxiang and Dasan Pass to cut off the enemy's route, Guan Shigu and others to gather Xihe troops at Datang in Minzhou, Sun Wo, Jia Shifang and others to gather Jingyuan and Fengxiang troops at the three prefectures of Jie, Cheng, and Feng to secure the Shu passes.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Wu Jie to gather troops and hold the dangerous ground at Monk's Plain near Fengxiang and at Dasan Pass to cut off the enemy's route; Guan Shigu and others to gather Xihe troops at Datang in Minzhou; and Sun Wo, Jia Shifang, and others to gather Jingyuan and Fengxiang troops in the three prefectures of Jie, Cheng, and Feng to secure the passes into Shu.

sentences.zh: 浚上書待罪，帝手詔慰勉。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; the emperor sent a hand edict to console and encourage him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; the emperor sent a hand edict to console and encourage him.

sentences.zh: 浚在關陝三年，訓新集之兵，當方張之敵，以劉子羽為上賓，任趙開為都轉運使，擢吳玠為大將守鳳翔。

translations.literal: Jun was in Guan-Shaan three years, trained newly gathered troops, faced enemies at full strength, took Liu Ziyu as chief guest, appointed Zhao Kai as Director of Transport, and promoted Wu Jie as great general defending Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun spent three years in Guan-Shaan, training newly gathered troops against enemies at the height of their power. He took Liu Ziyu as his chief adviser, appointed Zhao Kai Director of Transport, and promoted Wu Jie to great general defending Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 子羽慷慨有才略，開善理財，而玠每戰輒勝。

translations.literal: Ziyu was generous and possessed strategy; Kai was skilled at managing finances; and Jie won whenever he fought.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu was generous and possessed strategy; Kai was skilled at managing finances; and Jie won whenever he fought.

sentences.zh: 西北遺民，歸附日眾。

translations.literal: Remnant people of the northwest daily increased in those who came to join.
translations.idiomatic: Each day more remnant people of the northwest came to join them.

sentences.zh: 故關陝雖失，而全蜀按堵，且以形勢牽制東南，江、淮亦賴以安。

translations.literal: Thus though Guan-Shaan was lost, all of Shu remained secure, and by holding the strategic posture they tied down the southeast—the Yangtze and Huai also depended on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: Thus though Guan-Shaan was lost, all of Shu remained secure, and by holding this strategic posture they tied down the enemy in the southeast; the Yangtze and Huai regions also depended on this for their peace.

sentences.zh: 將軍曲端者，建炎中，嘗迫逐帥臣王庶而奪其印。

translations.literal: The general Qu Duan—during Jianyan had once chased and driven out commander Wang Shu and seized his seal.
translations.idiomatic: There was a general named Qu Duan who, during the Jianyan era, had once chased out the commander Wang Shu and seized his seal.

sentences.zh: 吳玠敗于彭原，訴端不整師。

translations.literal: When Wu Jie was defeated at Pengyuan, he accused Duan of not ordering the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Jie was defeated at Pengyuan, he accused Duan of failing to keep the army in order.

sentences.zh: 富平之役，端議不合，其腹心張忠彥等降敵。

translations.literal: At the Fu Ping campaign Duan's counsel did not agree; his intimate followers Zhang Zhongyan and others surrendered to the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: At the Fu Ping campaign Duan's counsel did not prevail, and his close followers Zhang Zhongyan and others surrendered to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 浚初超用端，中坐廢，猶欲再用之，後卒下端獄論死。

translations.literal: Jun had at first promoted Duan over others; midway he was dismissed; still he wished to use him again; in the end he put Duan in prison and sentenced him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had at first promoted Duan above others; midway Duan was dismissed, yet Jun still wished to employ him again; in the end he placed Duan in prison and sentenced him to death.

sentences.zh: 會有言浚殺趙哲、曲端無辜，而任子羽、開、玠非是，朝廷疑之。

translations.literal: When there were words that Jun killed Zhao Zhe and Qu Duan without cause while employing Ziyu, Kai, and Jie wrongly, the court grew doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: When word spread that Jun had killed Zhao Zhe and Qu Duan without cause while wrongly employing Ziyu, Kai, and Jie, the court grew doubtful.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣王似副浚。

translations.literal: In the third year they sent Wang Si as Jun's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year they sent Wang Si as Jun's deputy.

sentences.zh: 會金將撒離曷及劉豫叛黨聚兵入攻，破金州。

translations.literal: When the Jin general Sa Li Gai and Liu Yu's rebel faction gathered troops in attack, they took Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin general Sa Li Gai and the rebel faction of Liu Yu gathered their forces and attacked, they took Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 子羽為興元帥，約吳玠同守三泉。

translations.literal: Ziyu was commander of Xingyuan and agreed with Wu Jie jointly to hold Sanquan.
translations.idiomatic: Ziyu was commander of Xingyuan and agreed with Wu Jie to hold Sanquan together.

sentences.zh: 金人至金牛，宋師掩擊之，斬馘及墮溪谷死者，以數千計。

translations.literal: When the Jurchens reached Jiniu, Song forces ambushed them; those beheaded and those who fell into streams and ravines and died numbered in the thousands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jurchens reached Jiniu, Song forces ambushed them; those beheaded and those who fell into streams and ravines and died numbered in the thousands.

sentences.zh: 浚聞王似來，求解兵柄，且奏似不可任。

translations.literal: Jun heard Wang Si was coming, requested to relinquish military authority, and also memorialized that Si was not fit for the post.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun learned Wang Si was on his way, he asked to surrender his command of the army and also submitted a memorial stating that Si was unfit for the task.

sentences.zh: 宰相呂頤浩不悅，而朱勝非以宿憾日毀短浚，詔浚赴行在。

translations.literal: The chief councilor Lü Yihao was displeased, and Zhu Shengfei, owing to an old grudge, daily denigrated Jun; an edict ordered Jun to proceed to the imperial camp.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councilor Lü Yihao was displeased, and Zhu Shengfei, nursing an old grievance, daily spoke ill of Jun; the emperor ordered Jun to come to the imperial camp.

sentences.zh: 四年初，辛炳知潭州，浚在陝，以檄發兵，炳不遣，浚奏劾之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the fourth year, Xin Bing was prefect of Tan Prefecture; Jun was at Shaan and sent a dispatch to raise troops, but Bing did not send them; Jun memorialized impeaching him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the fourth year, Xin Bing was prefect of Tan Prefecture; Jun, then stationed in Shaan, issued a dispatch calling up troops, but Bing refused to send them, and Jun memorialized to impeach him.

sentences.zh: 至是，炳為御史中丞，率同列劾浚，以本官提舉洞霄宮，居福州。

translations.literal: At this time, Bing was censor-in-chief; he led his colleagues in impeaching Jun, who was given his original rank as superintendent of Dongxiao Palace and resided at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: By this time Bing had become censor-in-chief; he led his fellow officials in impeaching Jun, who was retained at his original rank as superintendent of Dongxiao Palace and sent to live in Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚既去國，慮金人釋川、陝之兵，必將並力窺東南，而朝廷已議講解，乃上疏極言其狀。

translations.literal: After Jun had left the court, he feared the Jurchens would release troops from Sichuan and Shaan and combine forces to probe the southeast, while the court was already debating peace talks, so he submitted a memorial urgently stating the situation.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jun had left court, he feared the Jurchens would redeploy their armies from Sichuan and Shaanxi to strike jointly at the southeast, even as the court was already debating a negotiated settlement, and he submitted an urgent memorial laying out the danger.

sentences.zh: 未幾，劉豫之子麟果引金人入攻。

translations.literal: Before long, Liu Yu's son Lin did indeed lead the Jurchens in an incursion.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Liu Yu's son Lin did indeed lead the Jurchens in an attack.

sentences.zh: 高宗思浚前言，策免朱勝非；

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong recalled Jun's earlier warning and by imperial decision dismissed Zhu Shengfei.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong recalled Jun's earlier warning and by policy decision dismissed Zhu Shengfei.

sentences.zh: 而參知政事趙鼎請幸平江，乃召浚以資政殿學士提舉萬壽觀兼侍讀。

translations.literal: The vice grand councilor Zhao Ding requested that the emperor visit Pingjiang; thereupon Jun was summoned as academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of Wanshou Temple, also serving as imperial reader.
translations.idiomatic: The vice grand councilor Zhao Ding urged the emperor to go to Pingjiang, and Jun was then recalled as academician of the Zizheng Hall and superintendent of Wanshou Temple, with the additional title of imperial reader.

sentences.zh: 入見，高宗手詔辨浚前誣，除知樞密院事。

translations.literal: On entering audience, Emperor Gaozong handed him an edict in the emperor's own writing clearing Jun of previous false accusations and appointed him director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When he was received in audience, Emperor Gaozong handed him a personal edict clearing him of prior false charges and appointed him director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 浚既受命，即日赴江上視師。

translations.literal: Once Jun had received the appointment, that very day he went to the river front to inspect the army.
translations.idiomatic: The day he received the appointment, Jun went straight to the Yangtze front to inspect the troops.

sentences.zh: 時兀術擁兵十萬於揚州，約日渡江決戰。

translations.literal: At the time Wuzhu held an army of a hundred thousand at Yangzhou and set a date to cross the river for decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wuzhu had a hundred thousand men at Yangzhou and had set a date to cross the river for a decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 浚長驅臨江，召韓世忠、張俊、劉光世議事。

translations.literal: Jun drove straight to the river, summoned Han Shizhong, Zhang Jun, and Liu Guangshi to consult.
translations.idiomatic: Jun pressed on to the river, summoned Han Shizhong, General Zhang Jun, and Liu Guangshi to consult.

sentences.zh: 將士見浚，勇氣十倍。

translations.literal: When the officers and soldiers saw Jun, their courage increased tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: When the officers and soldiers saw Jun, their fighting spirit increased tenfold.

sentences.zh: 浚既部分諸將，身留鎮江節度之。

translations.literal: Once Jun had assigned the various generals, he himself remained at Zhenjiang to command and regulate them.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jun had deployed the various generals, he himself remained at Zhenjiang to direct them.

sentences.zh: 世忠遣麾下王愈詣兀術約戰，且言張樞密已在鎮江。

translations.literal: Shizhong sent his subordinate Wang Yu to Wuzhu to arrange battle and said that Privy Councilor Zhang was already at Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shizhong sent his officer Wang Yu to Wuzhu to challenge him to battle, and said that Privy Councilor Zhang was already at Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 兀術曰：「張樞密貶嶺南，何得乃在此？」

translations.literal: Wuzhu said: "Privy Councilor Zhang was banished to Lingnan—how is he here?"
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu said, "Privy Councilor Zhang was exiled to Lingnan—how can he be here?"

sentences.zh: 愈出浚所下文書示之。

translations.literal: Yu produced the document Jun had issued and showed it to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu produced the document Jun had issued and showed it to him.

sentences.zh: 兀術色變，夕遁。

translations.literal: Wuzhu's color changed, and at night he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzhu's expression changed, and that night he fled.

sentences.zh: 五年，除尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼知樞密院事，都督諸路軍馬，趙鼎除左僕射。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Manager of Affairs under the Gate with the Secretariat-Chancellery and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Grand Commander of all circuit armies; Zhao Ding was appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Co-Manager of Affairs under the Gate with the Secretariat-Chancellery, and director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with overall command of all circuit armies; Zhao Ding was appointed Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 浚與鼎同志輔治，務在塞幸門，抑近習。

translations.literal: Jun and Ding shared the same purpose in assisting governance, striving to block the gate of imperial favor and restrain close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Ding worked together in the same spirit to govern, working to close off channels of imperial favoritism and restrain the emperor's close attendants.

sentences.zh: 時巨寇楊麼據洞庭，屢攻不克，浚以建康東南都會，而洞庭據上流，恐滋蔓為害，請因盛夏乘其怠討之，具奏請行。

translations.literal: At the time the great bandit Yang Yao held Dongting; repeated attacks had not overcome him; Jun considered that Jiankang was the metropolis of the southeast and Dongting controlled the upper reaches, fearing spread and harm, requested taking advantage of midsummer while they were slack to campaign against them, fully memorialized and requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the great bandit Yang Yao held Dongting Lake; repeated attacks had failed to subdue him; Jun judged that Jiankang was the capital of the southeast while Dongting controlled the upper Yangtze, and fearing the rebellion might spread, he asked to strike while they were slack in midsummer, submitting a full memorial requesting to lead the campaign.

sentences.zh: 至醴陵，釋邑囚數百，皆楊麼諜者，給以文書，俾招諭諸砦，囚歡呼而往。

translations.literal: Reaching Liling, he released several hundred county prisoners, all agents of Yang Yao, gave them documents, and had them summon and persuade the various strongholds; the prisoners went off with shouts of joy.
translations.idiomatic: At Liling he released several hundred county prisoners, all Yang Yao's agents, gave them written orders to summon and persuade the various strongholds, and the prisoners went off shouting with joy.

sentences.zh: 至潭，賊眾二十余萬相繼來降，湖寇盡平。

translations.literal: Reaching Tan Prefecture, over two hundred thousand bandits successively came to surrender; the lake bandits were completely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Tan Prefecture, more than two hundred thousand rebels successively surrendered, and the lake bandits were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 上賜浚書，謂：「上流既定，則川陝、荊襄形勢接連，事力增倍，天其以中興之功付卿乎。」

translations.literal: The emperor sent Jun a letter saying: "Once the upper reaches are settled, then the strategic positions of Sichuan-Shaan and Jing-Xiang will connect, strength will double—is Heaven about to entrust the task of revival to you?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote Jun, saying, "Once the upper Yangtze is secure, the positions in Sichuan-Shaan and Jing-Xiang will link up and our strength will double—is Heaven perhaps entrusting the task of restoration to you?"

sentences.zh: 浚遂奏遣岳飛屯荊、襄以圖中原，乃自鄂、嶽轉淮東，大會諸將，議防秋之宜。

translations.literal: Jun then memorialized dispatching Yue Fei to garrison Jing and Xiang to plan recovery of the Central Plains; then from Ezhou and Yuezhou he turned to Huai East, held a great assembly of generals, and discussed measures for autumn defense.
translations.idiomatic: Jun then memorialized dispatching Yue Fei to garrison Jing and Xiang to plan the recovery of the Central Plains; he himself went from Ezhou and Yuezhou to Huaidong, held a grand council of generals, and discussed measures for autumn defense.

sentences.zh: 高宗遣使賜詔趣歸，勞問之曰：「卿暑行甚勞，湖湘群寇既就招撫，成朕不殺之仁，卿之功也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong sent an envoy with an edict urging his return, inquiring after him and saying: "You have traveled hard in the summer heat; the bandits of Hunan and Hubei have been brought to submission by persuasion, fulfilling my virtue of not killing—this is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong sent an envoy with an edict urging his return and said in praise, "Your summer march has been arduous; the bandits of Hunan and Hubei have been brought to submission without bloodshed, fulfilling my wish to show mercy—this is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 召對便殿，進《中興備覽》四十一篇，高宗嘉歎，置之坐隅。

translations.literal: He was summoned for audience in the side hall and presented "Forty-one Chapters of Reference for Revival"; Emperor Gaozong praised it with admiration and placed it at the corner of his seat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience in the side hall and presented his Forty-one Chapters of Reference for Revival; Emperor Gaozong praised it warmly and kept it at his side.

sentences.zh: 浚以敵勢未衰，而叛臣劉豫復據中原，六年，會諸將議事江上，榜豫僭逆之罪。

translations.literal: Jun considered enemy strength had not declined and the rebel minister Liu Yu again held the Central Plains; in the sixth year he gathered the generals on the river to discuss affairs and posted a proclamation of Liu Yu's usurpation and treason.
translations.idiomatic: Judging that the enemy was still strong and the rebel Liu Yu again held the Central Plains, Jun in the sixth year gathered the generals on the Yangtze to discuss strategy and posted a proclamation listing Liu Yu's crimes of usurpation and rebellion.

sentences.zh: 命韓世忠據承、楚以圖淮陽；

translations.literal: He ordered Han Shizhong to hold Cheng and Chu to plan Huaiyang.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Han Shizhong to hold Cheng and Chu prefectures and press toward Huaiyang.

sentences.zh: 命劉光世屯合肥以招北軍；

translations.literal: He ordered Liu Guangshi to garrison at Hefei to recruit northern armies.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Liu Guangshi to encamp at Hefei to recruit troops from the north.

sentences.zh: 命張俊練兵建康，進屯盱眙；

translations.literal: He ordered Zhang Jun to drill troops at Jiankang and advance to garrison at Xuyi.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered General Zhang Jun to drill troops at Jiankang and advance to Xuyi.

sentences.zh: 命楊沂中領精兵為後翼以佐俊；

translations.literal: He ordered Yang Yizhong to lead elite troops as rear wing to assist Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Yizhong to lead elite troops as a rear guard to support Zhang Jun.

sentences.zh: 命岳飛進屯襄陽以窺中原。

translations.literal: He ordered Yue Fei to advance and garrison at Xiangyang to watch the Central Plains.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yue Fei to advance to Xiangyang and watch for an opportunity to strike into the Central Plains.

sentences.zh: 浚渡江，遍撫淮上諸戍。

translations.literal: Jun crossed the river and everywhere comforted the garrisons along the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Jun crossed the river and went among all the garrisons along the Huai to encourage the troops.

sentences.zh: 時張俊軍進屯盱眙，岳飛遣兵入至蔡州，浚入覲，力請幸建康。

translations.literal: At the time Zhang Jun's army had advanced to garrison at Xuyi; Yue Fei sent troops inward to reach Cai Prefecture; Jun entered audience and vigorously requested the emperor visit Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time General Zhang Jun's army had advanced to Xuyi; Yue Fei sent troops as far inland as Cai Prefecture; Jun went to audience and strongly urged the emperor to go to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 車駕進發，浚先往江上，諜報劉豫與侄猊挾金人入攻，浚奏：「金人不敢悉眾而來，此必豫兵也。」

translations.literal: The imperial carriage set out; Jun went ahead to the river front; spies reported Liu Yu and his nephew Ni were leading Jurchens in attack; Jun memorialized: "The Jurchens would not dare come with their full host—this must be Yu's troops."
translations.idiomatic: The imperial carriage set out; Jun went ahead to the river; spies reported that Liu Yu and his nephew Ni were leading Jurchen forces in an attack; Jun memorialized, "The Jurchens would not dare bring their full strength—this must be Liu Yu's army."

sentences.zh: 邊遽不一，俊、光世皆張大敵勢，浚謂：「賊豫以逆犯順，不剿除何以為國？

translations.literal: Reports from the border were inconsistent; Zhang Jun and Guangshi both exaggerated enemy strength; Jun said: "The bandit Yu rebels against obedience—how can we be a state without eliminating him?
translations.idiomatic: Border reports were conflicting; Zhang Jun and Guangshi both exaggerated the enemy force; Jun said, "The rebel Liu Yu has risen in rebellion against the throne—how can we remain a state without destroying him?

sentences.zh: 今日之事，有進無退。」

translations.literal: Today's affair allows advance, not retreat."
translations.idiomatic: In today's affair there is only advance, no retreat."

sentences.zh: 且命楊沂中往屯濠州。

translations.literal: And he ordered Yang Yizhong to go garrison at Haozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Yang Yizhong to encamp at Haozhou.

sentences.zh: 劉麟逼合肥，張俊請益兵，劉光世欲退師，趙鼎及簽書折彥質欲召岳飛兵東下。

translations.literal: Liu Lin pressed Hefei; Zhang Jun requested reinforcements; Liu Guangshi wished to withdraw troops; Zhao Ding and Secretary Zhe Yanzhi wished to summon Yue Fei's troops eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Lin pressed on Hefei; General Zhang Jun asked for reinforcements; Liu Guangshi wanted to withdraw; Zhao Ding and the secretary Zhe Yanzhi wanted to call Yue Fei's army east.

sentences.zh: 禦書付浚，令俊、光世、沂中等還保江。

translations.literal: An imperial letter was delivered to Jun ordering Zhang Jun, Guangshi, Yizhong, and others to return and hold the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial letter was handed to Jun ordering Zhang Jun, Guangshi, Yizhong, and the others to fall back and defend the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 浚奏：「俊等渡江，則無淮南，而長江之險與敵共矣。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized: "If Jun and the others cross the river, there will be no Huai South, and the Yangtze's strategic advantage will be shared with the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized, "If Zhang Jun and the others cross the river, we lose Huainan, and the Yangtze's defensive advantage will be shared with the enemy.

sentences.zh: 且岳飛一動，襄、漢有警，復何所恃乎？」

translations.literal: Moreover, if Yue Fei moves, Jing and Han will be alarmed—on what then would we rely?"
translations.idiomatic: And if Yue Fei moves, Jing and Han will be exposed—what would we have left to rely on?"

sentences.zh: 詔書從之。

translations.literal: The edict followed his view.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's order followed his advice.

sentences.zh: 沂中兵抵濠州，光世舍廬州而南，淮西洶動。

translations.literal: Yizhong's troops reached Haozhou; Guangshi abandoned Luzhou and went south; western Huai was in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhong's troops reached Haozhou, but Guangshi abandoned Luzhou and withdrew south, throwing western Huai into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 浚聞，疾馳至採石，令其眾曰：「有一人渡江者斬！」

translations.literal: When Jun heard, he galloped swiftly to Caishi and commanded his troops: "Whoever crosses the river—behead him!"
translations.idiomatic: When Jun heard, he raced to Caishi and ordered his men, "Anyone who crosses the river will be executed!"

sentences.zh: 光世復駐軍，與沂中接。

translations.literal: Guangshi again halted his army and linked with Yizhong.
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi halted his retreat and rejoined Yizhong.

sentences.zh: 劉猊攻沂中，沂中大破之，猊、麟皆拔柵遁。

translations.literal: Liu Ni attacked Yizhong; Yizhong heavily defeated him; Ni and Lin both uprooted their palisades and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ni attacked Yizhong; Yizhong routed him; Ni and Lin both broke camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 高宗手書嘉獎，召浚還，勞之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong wrote in his own hand with praise and reward, summoned Jun back, and commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong wrote a letter of praise in his own hand, recalled Jun, and commended him.

sentences.zh: 時趙鼎等議回蹕臨安，浚奏：「天下之事，不倡則不起，三歲之間，陛下一再臨江，士氣百倍。

translations.literal: At the time Zhao Ding and others debated returning the imperial progress to Lin'an; Jun memorialized: "Under Heaven, if nothing is initiated it will not rise; within three years Your Majesty has twice come to the river—morale is a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhao Ding and others urged returning the court to Lin'an; Jun memorialized, "Nothing in the empire moves unless someone leads the way; in three years Your Majesty has twice gone to the Yangtze front, and morale has risen a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 今六飛一還，人心解體。」

translations.literal: Now if the imperial carriage returns once, hearts of men will dissolve."
translations.idiomatic: But if the imperial carriage turns back now, the people's resolve will collapse."

sentences.zh: 高宗幡然從浚計。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong suddenly turned and followed Jun's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong changed his mind and followed Jun's plan.

sentences.zh: 鼎出知紹興府。

translations.literal: Ding went out to serve as prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was transferred out to serve as prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 浚以親民之官，治道所急，條具郡守、監司、省郎、館閣出入迭補之法；

translations.literal: Jun considered that officials close to the people were urgent to good governance, and set forth in detail the method of rotation and succession for prefects, supervisory commissioners, secretaries in the departments, and academicians in the institutes.
translations.idiomatic: Jun held that officials who serve the people directly are essential to good government, and laid out in detail a system of rotation for prefects, circuit commissioners, department secretaries, and institute scholars.

sentences.zh: 又以災異奏復賢良方正科。

translations.literal: He also memorialized, citing calamities and portents, to restore the xianliang examination.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized, citing omens and natural disasters, for restoration of the xianliang and fangzheng examinations.

sentences.zh: 七年，以浚卻敵功，制除特進。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, for Jun's merit in repelling the enemy, by imperial order he was specially promoted to tejin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, for his service in repelling the enemy, Jun was specially promoted to tejin.

sentences.zh: 未幾，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Before long, he was given the added title of Grandee of the Golden Purple Robe.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was given the additional title of Grandee of the Golden Purple Robe.

sentences.zh: 問安使何蘚歸報徽宗皇帝、甯德皇后相繼崩殂，上號慟擗踴，哀不自勝。

translations.literal: The envoy to inquire after their welfare, He Xian, returned reporting that Emperor Huizong and Empress Dowager Ningde had successively died; the emperor wailed and stamped and beat his breast in grief, sorrow beyond self-control.
translations.idiomatic: The welfare envoy He Xian returned with word that Emperor Huizong and Empress Dowager Ningde had died in succession; the emperor wailed and stamped in grief, overcome with sorrow.

sentences.zh: 浚奏：「天子之孝，不與士庶同，必思所以奉宗廟社稷，今梓宮未返，天下塗炭，願陛下揮涕而起，斂發而趨，一怒以安天下之民。」

translations.literal: Jun memorialized: "The Son of Heaven's filial piety is not the same as commoners'; he must consider how to serve the ancestral shrines and the altars of soil and grain; now the imperial coffins have not returned, the empire is in charred ruin—may Your Majesty wipe away tears and rise, restrain mourning and press forward, and with one burst of anger pacify the people under Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized, "The emperor's filial duty is not like that of common people; he must think of how to serve the ancestral shrines and the altars of state. The imperial coffins have not yet returned, and the realm is in ruins. I beg Your Majesty to wipe away your tears, rise up, set aside private mourning, and with righteous anger bring peace to the people."

sentences.zh: 上乃命浚草詔告諭中外，辭甚哀切。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered Jun to draft an edict proclaiming and instructing within and without; the language was very mournful and urgent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered Jun to draft an edict to announce the news at home and abroad; the language was deeply mournful and urgent.

sentences.zh: 浚又請命諸大將率三軍發哀成服，中外感動。

translations.literal: Jun also requested ordering the great generals to lead the three armies to begin mourning and wear mourning garb; within and without were moved.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also asked that the great generals be ordered to lead the three armies in assuming mourning dress; the court and the country were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 浚退上疏曰：「陛下思慕兩宮，憂勞百姓。

translations.literal: Jun withdrew and submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty yearns for the Two Palaces and worries over the hundred surnames.
translations.idiomatic: After withdrawing, Jun submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty grieves for the Two Palaces and bears the suffering of the people.

sentences.zh: 臣之至愚，獲遭任用，臣每感慨自期，誓殲敵仇。

translations.literal: This minister's utmost foolishness has met with appointment; I each time sigh and set expectations for myself, swearing to destroy the enemy in vengeance.
translations.idiomatic: Though I am most unworthy, I have been given office; I have always resolved in my heart to destroy the enemy and avenge this humiliation.

sentences.zh: 十年之間，親養闕然，爰及妻孥，莫之私顧，其意亦欲遂陛下孝養之心，拯生民於塗炭。

translations.literal: For ten years, personal care for parents has been lacking; extending even to wife and children, I have not looked to private affairs—the intent also was to fulfill Your Majesty's filial heart and rescue the living people from charred ruin.
translations.idiomatic: For ten years I have neglected my own parents, and even my wife and children I have not tended in private—my aim was to fulfill Your Majesty's filial wishes and rescue the people from ruin.

sentences.zh: 昊天不吊，禍變忽生，使陛下抱無窮之痛，罪將誰執。

translations.literal: High Heaven does not pity; calamity suddenly arose, causing Your Majesty to embrace endless pain—whose fault shall be held?
translations.idiomatic: Heaven showed no mercy; disaster struck suddenly, leaving Your Majesty with boundless grief—who is to blame?

sentences.zh: 念昔陝、蜀之行，陛下命臣曰：'我有大隙於北，刷此至恥，惟爾是屬。

translations.literal: Recalling the journey to Shaan and Shu, Your Majesty commanded this minister, saying: 'I bear a great rift with the north; to wipe away this utmost shame—I entrust it only to you.'
translations.idiomatic: I recall that when you sent me to Shaan and Shu, Your Majesty commanded me, saying, 'I bear a great debt to the north and must wipe away this deepest shame—I entrust this task to you alone.'

sentences.zh: '而臣終隳成功，使敵無憚，今日之禍，端自臣致，乞賜罷黜。」

translations.literal: Yet this minister ultimately destroyed success, causing the enemy to fear nothing; today's disaster originated in what I brought about—I beg to be dismissed and removed."
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the end I ruined our success, leaving the enemy without fear. Today's disaster began with me—I beg to be dismissed."

sentences.zh: 上詔浚起視事。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict to Jun to rise and resume affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Jun to rise and resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 浚再疏待罪，不許，乃請乘輿發平江，至建康。

translations.literal: Jun again memorialized accepting blame; this was not permitted; he then requested the imperial carriage set out from Pingjiang to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted another memorial accepting blame; this too was refused; he then urged the imperial carriage to leave Pingjiang for Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 浚總中外之政，幾事叢委，以一身任之。

translations.literal: Jun oversaw government at home and abroad; affairs clustered thickly and he bore them with one body.
translations.idiomatic: Jun oversaw both civil and military affairs; business piled up in profusion, and he bore it all on his own shoulders.

sentences.zh: 每奏對，必言仇恥之大，反復再三，上未嘗不改容流涕。

translations.literal: At each audience memorial, he always spoke of the greatness of enmity and shame, repeatedly again and again; the emperor never failed to change expression and weep.
translations.idiomatic: At every audience he spoke again and again of the enormity of the national shame and humiliation, and the emperor never failed to change expression and weep.

sentences.zh: 時天子方厲精克己，戒飭宮庭內侍，無敢越度，事無巨細，必以咨浚，賜諸將詔，往往命浚草之。

translations.literal: At the time the Son of Heaven was vigorously refining himself, restraining himself, warning and correcting palace eunuchs—none dared exceed bounds; affairs whether large or small, he always consulted Jun; edicts bestowed on generals were often ordered drafted by Jun.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was striving to discipline himself, tightening rules for palace eunuchs so that none dared overstep; he consulted Jun on matters large and small, and edicts to the generals were often drafted by Jun.

sentences.zh: 劉光世在淮西，軍無紀律，浚奏罷光世，以其兵屬督府，命參謀兵部尚書呂祉往廬州節制。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi was in western Huai; the army had no discipline; Jun memorialized dismissing Guangshi, placing his troops under the supervisory headquarters, and ordered staff officer Minister of War Lü Zhi to go to Luzhou to command and regulate them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi was in western Huai, where his army had no discipline; Jun memorialized to remove him, placed his troops under the headquarters, and sent staff officer Lü Zhi, minister of war, to Luzhou to take command.

sentences.zh: 而樞密院以督府握兵為嫌，乞置武帥，乃以王德為都統制，即軍中取酈瓊副之。

translations.literal: But the Bureau of Military Affairs, taking the supervisory headquarters' control of troops as objectionable, requested placing a military commander; thereupon Wang De was made overall commander, and Li Qiong was taken from the army as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: But the Bureau of Military Affairs objected to the headquarters holding direct command of troops and requested a military commander; Wang De was made overall commander, with Li Qiong taken from the ranks as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 浚奏其不當，瓊亦與德有宿怨，列狀訴御史台，乃命張俊為宣撫使，楊沂中、劉錡為制置判官以撫之。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized that this was improper; Qiong also had an old grudge with De and submitted a written complaint to the Censorate; thereupon Zhang Jun was made pacification commissioner, and Yang Yizhong and Liu Qi were made deputy commissioners for arrangement to mollify them.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized that this was wrong; Qiong also had an old grievance against De and filed a complaint with the censorate; General Zhang Jun was then made pacification commissioner, with Yang Yizhong and Liu Qi as deputies to settle the troops.

sentences.zh: 未至，瓊等舉軍叛，執呂祉以歸劉豫。

translations.literal: Before they arrived, Qiong and others rose with the whole army in rebellion, seized Lü Zhi and took him back to Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Before they arrived, Qiong and the others mutinied with the whole army, seized Lü Zhi, and delivered him to Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 祉不行，詈瓊等，碎齒折首而死。

translations.literal: Zhi would not go; he cursed Qiong and the others; his teeth were shattered and his neck broken—he died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi refused to go; he cursed Qiong and the others; they smashed his teeth and broke his neck, and he died.

sentences.zh: 浚引咎求去位，高宗問可代者，且曰：「秦檜何如？」

translations.literal: Jun accepted blame and requested leaving office; Emperor Gaozong asked who could replace him and said: "What of Qin Hui?"
translations.idiomatic: Jun accepted the blame and asked to leave office; Emperor Gaozong asked who might replace him and said, "What about Qin Hui?"

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「近與共事，方知其暗。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "Having recently worked together, only now I know he is secretive."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "Having worked with him recently, I have only now seen how underhanded he is."

sentences.zh: 高宗曰：「然則用趙鼎。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong said: "Then employ Zhao Ding."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong said, "Then we shall use Zhao Ding."

sentences.zh: 檜由是憾浚。

translations.literal: Hui thereby bore resentment toward Jun.
translations.idiomatic: From this Qin Hui came to resent Jun.

sentences.zh: 浚以觀文殿大學士提舉江州太平興國宮。

translations.literal: Jun was given the title of academician of the Guanwen Hall and made superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was made academician of the Guanwen Hall and superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，浚遣人持手榜入偽地間劉豫，及酈瓊叛去，復遣間持蠟書遺瓊，金人果疑豫，尋廢之。

translations.literal: Previously, Jun had sent men with a hand-written placard into the puppet territory to sow discord against Liu Yu; when Li Qiong rebelled and left, he again sent agents bearing sealed letters to Qiong; the Jurchens indeed grew suspicious of Yu and soon deposed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Jun had sent agents with handwritten messages into enemy territory to sow distrust of Liu Yu; when Li Qiong defected, he sent agents with sealed letters to Qiong; the Jurchens did indeed grow suspicious of Liu Yu and soon deposed him.

sentences.zh: 台諫交詆，浚落職，以秘書少監分司西京，居永州。

translations.literal: Censors and remonstrators alternately denounced him; Jun was demoted from office, given the rank of vice director of the Secretariat as a nominal post in the Western Capital, and resided at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The censors and remonstrators attacked him in turn; Jun was stripped of rank, given the nominal post of vice director of the Secretariat at the Western Capital, and sent to live in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 九年，以赦復官。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, by amnesty his rank was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year his rank was restored by amnesty.

sentences.zh: 提舉臨安府洞霄宮。

translations.literal: He was made superintendent of Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was made superintendent of Dongxiao Palace in Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，除資政殿大學士、知福州兼福建安撫大使。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall, prefect of Fuzhou, and concurrently Grand Pacification Commissioner of Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall, prefect of Fuzhou, and concurrently grand pacification commissioner of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 金遣使來，以詔諭為名，浚五上疏爭之。

translations.literal: The Jin sent envoys who, under the name of imperial proclamation and instruction, came; Jun five times submitted memorials objecting.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent envoys under the guise of delivering an imperial proclamation; Jun submitted five memorials objecting.

sentences.zh: 十年，金敗盟，復取河南。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Jin broke the treaty and again took Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the Jin broke the treaty and retook Henan.

sentences.zh: 浚奏願因權制變，則大勳可集，因大治海舟千艘，為直指山東之計。

translations.literal: Jun memorialized wishing to adapt to circumstances and seize changing conditions, then great merit could be gathered; accordingly he greatly prepared a thousand sea-going vessels as a plan to strike straight at Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Jun memorialized that if they seized the moment and adapted to circumstances, great achievements could be won; he accordingly had a thousand seagoing vessels built in preparation for a direct strike at Shandong.

sentences.zh: 十一年，除檢校少傅、崇信軍節度使，充萬壽觀使，免奉朝請。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, he was appointed Honorary Junior Mentor, military commissioner of Chongxin Army, and made superintendent of Wanshou Temple, exempt from court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was appointed honorary junior mentor, military commissioner of the Chongxin Army, and superintendent of Wanshou Temple, exempt from court attendance.

sentences.zh: 十二年，封和國公。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was enfeoffed as Duke of Heguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was enfeoffed as Duke of Heguo.

sentences.zh: 十六年，彗星出西方，浚將極論時事，恐貽母憂。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, a comet appeared in the west; Jun was about to speak fully on current affairs and feared causing his mother worry.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year a comet appeared in the west; Jun was about to speak out forcefully on current affairs but feared distressing his mother.

sentences.zh: 母訝其瘠，問故，浚以實對。

translations.literal: His mother was surprised at his thinness, asked the reason; Jun answered truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was alarmed at how thin he had grown, asked why, and Jun told her the truth.

sentences.zh: 母誦其父對策之語曰：「臣甯言而死於斧鉞，不能忍不言以負陛下。」

translations.literal: His mother recited the words from his father's examination response: "This minister would rather speak and die under axe and halberd than endure silence and fail Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: His mother recited words from his father's examination answer: "I would rather speak and die under the executioner's axe than keep silent and fail Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 浚意乃決。

translations.literal: Jun's resolve was then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 上疏謂：「當今事勢，譬如養成大疽于頭目心腹之間，不決不止。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial saying: "Today's situation is like a great ulcer nurtured between head, eyes, and heart-and-belly—if not cut out it will not stop.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial saying, "The situation today is like a great abscess growing between the head, eyes, and heart—unless it is cut out, it will not stop.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下謀之于心，謹察情偽，使在我有不可犯之勢，庶幾社稷安全；

translations.literal: Only may Your Majesty plan in the heart, carefully examine truth and falsehood, so that on our side there is an inviolable position—then perhaps the altars of soil and grain will be secure.
translations.idiomatic: Only if Your Majesty deliberates in your heart, carefully discerns truth from pretense, and secures a position the enemy cannot violate will the altars of state perhaps be secure.

sentences.zh: 不然，後將噬臍。」

translations.literal: Otherwise, later one will bite one's own navel."
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, you will later bite your own navel in regret."

sentences.zh: 事下三省，秦檜大怒，令台諫論浚，以特進提舉江州太平興國宮，居連州。

translations.literal: The matter was sent down to the Three Departments; Qin Hui was greatly enraged, ordered the censorate and remonstrators to criticize Jun; he was given tejin as superintendent of Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou and resided at Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was referred to the Three Departments; Qin Hui was furious and had the censors attack Jun; Jun was reduced to tejin as superintendent of the Taiping Xingguo Palace in Jiangzhou and sent to live in Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，徙永州。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was transferred to Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year he was transferred to Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚去國幾二十載，天下士無賢不肖，莫不傾心慕之。

translations.literal: Jun had been away from court for nearly twenty years; scholars throughout the realm, whether worthy or not, all turned their hearts to admire him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had been out of office for nearly twenty years, and men of learning throughout the realm—worthy or unworthy alike—all looked to him with admiration.

sentences.zh: 武夫健將，言浚者必咨嗟太息，至兒童婦女，亦知有張都督也。

translations.literal: Bold warriors and strong generals, speaking of Jun, invariably sighed deeply; even children and women knew of Director-General Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Bold warriors and seasoned generals, whenever they spoke of Jun, sighed with deep feeling; even children and women knew the name of Director-General Zhang.

sentences.zh: 金人憚浚，每使至，必問浚安在，惟恐其復用。

translations.literal: The Jurchens feared Jun; whenever their envoys arrived, they invariably asked where Jun was, dreading his return to office.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens feared Jun; whenever their envoys came, they always asked where he was, dreading his return to power.

sentences.zh: 當是時，秦檜怙寵固位，懼浚為正論以害己，令台臣有所彈劾，論必及浚，反謂浚為國賊，必欲殺之。

translations.literal: At that time Qin Hui, relying on favor to hold his position, feared Jun's righteous arguments would harm him; he had censorate officials launch accusations, and whenever they criticized, they always implicated Jun, even calling Jun a traitor to the state and determined to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Qin Hui, secure in imperial favor, feared that Jun's upright arguments would threaten him; he had censorate officials bring accusations, and every attack inevitably touched on Jun—going so far as to call him a traitor to the state and set out to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 以張柄知潭州，汪召錫使湖南，使圖浚。

translations.literal: He appointed Zhang Bing prefect of Tanzhou and dispatched Wang Zhaoxi as envoy to Hunan to devise a plot against Jun.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Zhang Bing prefect of Tanzhou and sent Wang Zhaoxi as envoy to Hunan to plot against Jun.

sentences.zh: 張常先使江西，治張宗元獄，株連及浚，捕趙鼎子汾下大理，令自誣與浚謀大逆，會檜死乃免。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang was first sent to Jiangxi to try the Zhang Zongyuan case, implicating Jun by extension; they arrested Zhao Ding's son Fen and sent him to the Office of the Chief Law Enforcement Officer, forcing him to falsely confess plotting great treason with Jun; only when Qin died was he spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang was first sent to Jiangxi to try the Zhang Zongyuan case, which by extension implicated Jun; Zhao Ding's son Fen was arrested and sent to the Office of the Chief Law Enforcement Officer and forced to falsely confess that he and Jun had plotted treason—only Qin's death spared him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，復觀文殿大學士、判洪州。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was restored as Grandee of the Hall for Promoting Literature and given concurrent charge of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he was restored as Grandee of the Hall for Promoting Literature and given charge of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚時以母喪將歸葬。

translations.literal: Jun was at that time returning to bury his mother in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was then in mourning for his mother and about to return home for the burial.

sentences.zh: 念天下事二十年為檜所壞，邊備蕩馳；

translations.literal: Reflecting that affairs of the realm had been ruined by Qin for twenty years and frontier defenses had been thrown into disorder;
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting that Qin had ruined the affairs of the realm for twenty years and that frontier defenses had been utterly neglected,

sentences.zh: 又聞金亮篡立，必將舉兵，自以大臣，義同休戚，不敢以居喪為嫌，具奏論之。

translations.literal: and hearing that Wanyan Liang had usurped the throne and would surely raise troops, he considered himself a great minister bound to the state in weal and woe, and dared not use mourning as a pretext for silence; he submitted a full memorial discussing the matter.
translations.idiomatic: and hearing that Wanyan Liang had seized the throne and would surely raise an army, he considered himself a great minister who shared the state's fortune and misfortune alike and dared not use mourning as an excuse for silence; he submitted a full memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 會星變求直言，浚謂金人數年間，勢決求釁用兵，而國家溺于宴安，蕩然無備，乃上疏極言。

translations.literal: When a celestial anomaly prompted a call for frank speech, Jun said the Jurchens within a few years would surely seek a pretext for war; yet the state was sunk in banquets and ease and wholly unprepared—he submitted a memorial speaking out with full force.
translations.idiomatic: When a celestial anomaly prompted the court to seek frank counsel, Jun argued that within a few years the Jurchens would surely seek a pretext for war, while the state was sunk in ease and wholly unprepared; he submitted a memorial speaking out with all his force.

sentences.zh: 而大臣沈該、萬俟禼、湯思退等見之，謂敵初無釁，笑浚為狂。
