translations.literal: But grand councillors Shen Gai, Wan Qixie, Tang Situi, and others who saw it said the enemy had no pretext at first and laughed at Jun as mad.
translations.idiomatic: But when grand councillors Shen Gai, Wan Qixie, Tang Situi, and others read it, they said the enemy had no pretext for war and laughed at Jun as a madman.

sentences.zh: 台諫湯鵬舉、淩哲論浚歸蜀，恐搖動遠方，詔復居永州。

translations.literal: Censors Tang Pengju and Ling Zhe argued that Jun's return to Sichuan might unsettle distant regions; an edict ordered him to reside again at Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Tang Pengju and Ling Zhe argued that Jun's return to Sichuan might unsettle distant regions, and an edict ordered him to reside again at Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 服除落職，以本官奉祠。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he lost office and served only with his former title in a temple post.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he was removed from active office and retained only his former title in a temple sinecure.

sentences.zh: 三十一年春，有旨自便。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-first year, an edict permitted him freedom of movement.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-first year an edict granted him freedom of movement.

sentences.zh: 浚至潭，聞欽宗崩，號慟不食，上疏請早定守戰之策。

translations.literal: When Jun reached Tan, he heard of Emperor Qinzong's death, wailed and refused food, and submitted a memorial urging early settlement of defensive and offensive strategy.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached Tanzhou he heard that Emperor Qinzong had died; he wailed in grief and refused food, and submitted a memorial urging the court to settle its strategy of defense and war without delay.

sentences.zh: 未幾，亮兵大入，中外震動，復浚觀文殿大學士、判潭州。

translations.literal: Before long, Liang's army invaded on a grand scale and the court and countryside were shaken; Jun was restored as Grandee of the Hall for Promoting Literature and given charge of Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Liang's army invaded on a great scale, shaking court and countryside alike; Jun was restored as Grandee of the Hall for Promoting Literature and given charge of Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時金騎充斥，王權兵潰，劉錡退歸鎮江，遂改命浚判建康府兼行宮留守。

translations.literal: At that time Jurchen cavalry filled the land; Wang Quan's army collapsed; Liu Qi withdrew to Zhenjiang—Jun's assignment was changed to judge Jiankang Prefecture concurrently serving as caretaker of the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jurchen horsemen filled the land; Wang Quan's army collapsed and Liu Qi withdrew to Zhenjiang; Jun was reassigned to judge Jiankang Prefecture and concurrently serve as caretaker of the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 浚至岳陽，買舟冒風雪而行，遇東來者云：「敵兵方焚採石，煙炎漲天，慎無輕進。」

translations.literal: Jun reached Yueyang, bought a boat and set out through wind and snow; meeting someone coming from the east who said: "The enemy is now burning Caishi—the smoke and flames fill the sky; beware of advancing lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Jun reached Yueyang, bought a boat, and set out through wind and snow; he met someone coming from the east who said, "The enemy is now burning Caishi—smoke and flames fill the sky. Do not advance rashly."

sentences.zh: 浚曰：「吾赴君父之急，知直前求乘輿所在而已。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "I go to meet my sovereign and father's urgency—I know only to press straight ahead and find where the imperial carriage is."
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied, "I go to answer my sovereign and father's urgent need—I need only press straight ahead and find where the imperial carriage is."

sentences.zh: 時長江無一舟敢行北岸者。

translations.literal: At that time on the Yangtze not a single boat dared sail the north bank.
translations.idiomatic: At that time not a single boat on the Yangtze dared sail the north bank.

sentences.zh: 浚乘小舟徑進，過池陽，聞亮死，餘眾猶二萬屯和州。

translations.literal: Jun took a small boat and pressed straight on; passing Chiyang he heard Liang was dead, but remnant forces of twenty thousand still encamped at Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun took a small boat and pressed straight on; passing Chiyang he heard that Liang was dead, but some twenty thousand remnant troops still encamped at Hezhou.

sentences.zh: 李顯忠兵在沙上，浚往犒之，一軍見浚，以為從天而下。

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong's troops were on the sandbanks; Jun went to reward them; the whole army seeing Jun took it as though he had descended from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong's troops were on the sandbanks; Jun went to reward them, and when the whole army saw him they felt as though he had descended from heaven.

sentences.zh: 浚至建康，即牒通判劉子昂辦行宮儀物，請乘輿亟臨幸。

translations.literal: Jun reached Jiankang, immediately dispatched a notice to Vice Prefect Liu Zi'ang to prepare traveling palace ceremonial objects, and requested the imperial carriage come at once.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun reached Jiankang he immediately sent a notice to Vice Prefect Liu Zi'ang to prepare the traveling palace's ceremonial accoutrements and urged the imperial carriage to come at once.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，車駕幸建康，浚迎拜道左，衛士見浚，無不以手加額。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, the imperial carriage visited Jiankang; Jun welcomed and bowed at the left of the road; the guards seeing Jun all placed their hands on their foreheads.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-second year the imperial carriage visited Jiankang; Jun welcomed it and bowed at the roadside, and the guards who saw him all raised their hands to their foreheads in reverence.

sentences.zh: 時浚起廢復用，風采隱然，軍民皆倚以為重。

translations.literal: At that time Jun had been recalled from disgrace and restored to office; his bearing was imposing, and soldiers and civilians alike relied on him as a pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had just been recalled from disgrace and restored to office; his presence was commanding, and soldiers and civilians alike looked to him as their mainstay.

sentences.zh: 車駕將還臨安，勞浚曰：「卿在此，朕無北顧憂矣。」

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to return to Lin'an, the emperor consoled Jun, saying: "With you here, I have no worry for the north."
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage was about to return to Lin'an, the emperor consoled Jun, saying, "With you here, I need not look back in worry toward the north."

sentences.zh: 兼節制建康、鎮江府、江州、池州、江陰軍軍馬。

translations.literal: He was also given overall command of the armies of Jiankang, Zhenjiang, Jiangzhou, Chizhou, and Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given overall command of the armies of Jiankang, Zhenjiang, Jiangzhou, Chizhou, and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 金兵十萬圍海州，浚命鎮江都統張子蓋往救，大破之。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand Jurchen troops besieged Haizhou; Jun ordered Zhenjiang commander Zhang Zigai to go to the rescue, and he inflicted a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When a hundred thousand Jurchen troops besieged Haizhou, Jun ordered Zhenjiang commander Zhang Zigai to the rescue, and he won a great victory.

sentences.zh: 浚招集忠義，及募淮楚壯勇，以陳敏為統制。

translations.literal: Jun gathered loyalists and recruited stalwart men from Huai and Chu, appointing Chen Min as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Jun gathered loyalists and recruited stalwart men from the Huai and Chu regions, appointing Chen Min as their commander.

sentences.zh: 且謂敵長於騎，我長於步，衛步莫如弩，衛弩莫如車，命敏專制弩治車。

translations.literal: He also said the enemy excelled at cavalry while they excelled at infantry; to protect infantry nothing matched crossbows, and to protect crossbows nothing matched chariots—he ordered Chen Min to take exclusive charge of crossbows and chariots.
translations.idiomatic: He also argued that the enemy excelled at cavalry while Song forces excelled at infantry; infantry were best protected by crossbows, and crossbows by chariots—he put Chen Min in sole charge of organizing crossbows and chariots.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，召浚入見，改容曰：「久聞公名，今朝廷所恃唯公。」

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozong ascended the throne, Jun was summoned for an audience; the emperor changed expression and said: "I have long heard your name; now the court relies on you alone."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozong took the throne, Jun was summoned for an audience; the emperor's manner changed as he said, "I have long heard your name—now the court relies on you alone."

sentences.zh: 賜坐降問，浚從容言：「人主之學，以心為本，一心合天，何事不濟？

translations.literal: He was granted a seat and questioned deferentially; Jun spoke calmly: "The learning of a ruler takes the heart as its root; when the single heart accords with Heaven, what affair will not succeed?
translations.idiomatic: He was granted a seat and questioned with deference; Jun answered calmly, "A ruler's learning takes the heart as its foundation; when the heart is one with Heaven, what task will not succeed?

sentences.zh: 所謂天者，天下之公理而已。

translations.literal: What is called Heaven is simply the public principle of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: What is called Heaven is simply the public principle of the realm.

sentences.zh: 必兢業自持，使清明在躬，則賞罰舉措，無有不當，人心自歸，敵仇自服。」

translations.literal: One must hold oneself in reverent diligence so that clarity and brightness are present in the person—then rewards and punishments and every measure will be fitting, hearts will return of themselves, and enemy foes will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Hold yourself in reverent diligence until clarity shines in your person—then rewards and punishments and every measure will be right, hearts will rally of their own accord, and enemies will submit of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 孝宗悚然曰：「當不忘公言。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong was startled and said: "I shall not forget your words."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong was startled and said, "I shall not forget what you have said."

sentences.zh: 除少傅、江淮東西路宣撫使，進封魏國公。

translations.literal: He was appointed Junior Mentor, Commissioner for Pacification of the Huai and Jiang East and West circuits, and advanced in enfeoffment to Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Junior Mentor and Commissioner for Pacification of the Huai and Jiang East and West circuits, and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士史浩議欲城瓜州、採石。

translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Shi Hao proposed fortifying Guazhou and Caishi.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin Academician Shi Hao proposed building fortifications at Guazhou and Caishi.

sentences.zh: 浚謂不守兩淮而守江幹，是示敵以削弱，怠戰守之氣，不若先城泗州。

translations.literal: Jun said that not holding the two Huai but defending the riverbank showed the enemy weakness and slackened the spirit of war and defense—it would be better first to fortify Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun argued that abandoning the two Huai and defending only the riverbank would show the enemy weakness and sap the will to fight and hold ground; it would be better to fortify Sizhou first.

sentences.zh: 及浩參知政事，浚所規畫，浩必沮之。

translations.literal: When Shi Hao became Vice Grand Councillor, he invariably obstructed whatever Jun planned.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shi Hao became Vice Grand Councillor, he invariably blocked whatever Jun planned.

sentences.zh: 浚薦陳俊卿為宣撫判官，孝宗召俊卿及浚子栻赴行在。

translations.literal: Jun recommended Chen Junqing as Pacification Commissioner's judge; Xiaozong summoned Chen Junqing and Jun's son Shi to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: Jun recommended Chen Junqing as judge on the Pacification Commission; Xiaozong summoned Chen Junqing and Jun's son Shi to the traveling court.

sentences.zh: 浚附奏請上臨幸建康，以動中原之心，用師淮堧，進舟山東，以為吳璘聲援。

translations.literal: Jun appended a memorial asking the emperor to visit Jiankang to stir the hearts of the Central Plain, deploy troops on the Huai frontier, and advance a fleet to Shandong as support for Wu Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Jun appended a memorial asking the emperor to visit Jiankang to stir the hearts of the Central Plain, deploy troops on the Huai frontier, and advance a fleet to Shandong to support Wu Lin.

sentences.zh: 孝宗見俊卿等，問浚動靜飲食顏貌，曰：「朕倚魏公如長城，不容浮言搖奪。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong saw Chen Junqing and the others and asked about Jun's movements, diet, and appearance, saying: "I rely on the Duke of Wei as on the Long Wall—I will not allow loose talk to shake my trust."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong saw Chen Junqing and the others and asked about Jun's movements, diet, and appearance, saying, "I rely on the Duke of Wei as on the Long Wall—I will not let loose talk shake my trust."

sentences.zh: 金人以十萬眾屯河南，聲言規兩淮，移文索海、泗、唐、鄧、商州及歲幣。

translations.literal: The Jurchens massed a hundred thousand men in Henan, proclaiming a plan against the two Huai, and sent a dispatch demanding Haizhou, Sizhou, Tangzhou, Dengzhou, Shangzhou, and the annual tribute.
translations.idiomatic: The Jurchens massed a hundred thousand men in Henan, proclaiming an intention to strike the two Huai, and sent a dispatch demanding Haizhou, Sizhou, Tangzhou, Dengzhou, Shangzhou, and the annual tribute.

sentences.zh: 浚言北敵詭詐，不當為之動，以大兵屯盱眙、濠、廬備之，卒以無事。

translations.literal: Jun said the northern foe was deceitful and the court should not be moved by it; he massed great armies at Xuyi, Hao, and Lu to prepare, and in the end nothing happened.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said the northern foe was deceitful and should not be heeded; he massed large forces at Xuyi, Hao, and Lu to meet them, and in the end nothing came of it.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，除樞密使，都督建康、鎮江府、江州、池州、江陰軍軍馬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing, he was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given overall command of the armies of Jiankang, Zhenjiang, Jiangzhou, Chizhou, and Jiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs and given overall command of the armies of Jiankang, Zhenjiang, Jiangzhou, Chizhou, and Jiangyin.

sentences.zh: 時金將蒲察徒穆及知泗州大周仁屯虹縣，都統蕭琦，屯靈壁，積糧修城，將為南攻計。

translations.literal: At that time Jurchen generals Pucha Tumo and Sizhou prefect Da Zhouren encamped at Hong County, and commander Xiao Qi encamped at Lingbi, storing grain and repairing walls in preparation for a southern attack.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Jurchen generals Pucha Tumo and Sizhou prefect Da Zhouren were encamped at Hong County, and commander Xiao Qi at Lingbi, storing grain and repairing walls in preparation for a southern attack.

sentences.zh: 浚欲及其未發攻之。

translations.literal: Jun wished to attack before they could launch their campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Jun wished to attack before they could launch their campaign.

sentences.zh: 會主管殿前司李顯忠、建康都統邵宏淵亦獻搗二邑之策，浚具以聞。

translations.literal: At the same time Director of the Palace Front Office Li Xianzhong and Jiankang commander Shao Hongyuan also submitted plans to strike the two towns; Jun reported this in full.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Director of the Palace Front Office Li Xianzhong and Jiankang commander Shao Hongyuan also submitted plans to strike the two towns; Jun reported the matter in full.

sentences.zh: 上報可，召浚赴行在，命先圖兩城。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and summoned Jun to the traveling court, ordering him first to take the two cities.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and summoned Jun to court, ordering him first to take the two cities.

sentences.zh: 乃遣顯忠出濠州，趨靈壁；

translations.literal: He then dispatched Li Xianzhong out from Haozhou toward Lingbi;
translations.idiomatic: He then sent Li Xianzhong out from Haozhou toward Lingbi;

sentences.zh: 宏淵出泗州，趨虹縣，而浚自往臨之。

translations.literal: Shao Hongyuan out from Sizhou toward Hong County, while Jun himself went to oversee the operation.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Hongyuan out from Sizhou toward Hong County, while Jun himself went to oversee the operation.

sentences.zh: 顯忠至靈壁，敗蕭琦；

translations.literal: Li Xianzhong reached Lingbi and defeated Xiao Qi;
translations.idiomatic: Li Xianzhong reached Lingbi and defeated Xiao Qi;

sentences.zh: 宏淵圍虹縣，降徒穆、周仁，乘勝進克宿州，中原震動。

translations.literal: Shao Hongyuan besieged Hong County and accepted the surrender of Tumo and Zhouren; pressing the victory they next captured Suzhou, and the Central Plain was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Hongyuan besieged Hong County and accepted the surrender of Tumo and Zhouren; pressing their victory they next captured Suzhou, and the Central Plain was shaken.

sentences.zh: 孝宗手書勞之曰：「近日邊報，中外鼓舞，十年來無此克捷。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong wrote in his own hand to commend them: "Recent frontier reports have stirred court and countryside alike—there has been no victory like this in ten years."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong wrote in his own hand to commend them: "Recent frontier reports have stirred court and countryside alike—there has been no victory like this in ten years."

sentences.zh: 浚以盛夏人疲，急召李顯忠等還師。

translations.literal: Jun, because men were weary in the height of summer, urgently recalled Li Xianzhong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Because the troops were exhausted in the height of summer, Jun urgently recalled Li Xianzhong and the others.

sentences.zh: 會金帥紇石烈志寧率兵至宿州，與顯忠戰。

translations.literal: Just then Jurchen commander Heshilie Zhining led troops to Suzhou and fought Li Xianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Jurchen commander Heshilie Zhining led troops to Suzhou and fought Li Xianzhong.

sentences.zh: 連日南軍小不利，忽諜報敵兵大至，顯忠夜引歸。

translations.literal: For several days the southern army met with small setbacks; suddenly a spy report came that enemy troops were arriving in force, and Li Xianzhong withdrew by night.
translations.idiomatic: For several days the southern army met with small setbacks; then a spy report came that enemy troops were arriving in force, and Li Xianzhong withdrew by night.

sentences.zh: 浚上疏待罪，有旨降授特進，更為江、淮宣撫使。

translations.literal: Jun submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; an edict demoted him to tejin and reappointed him Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Jun submitted a memorial awaiting punishment; an edict demoted him to tejin and reappointed him Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 宿師之還，士大夫主和者皆議浚之非，孝宗復賜浚書曰：「今日邊事倚卿為重，卿不可畏人言而懷猶豫。

translations.literal: When the troops at Suzhou withdrew, court scholars who favored peace all debated Jun's fault; Xiaozong again sent Jun a letter saying: "Today's frontier affairs rely on you above all—you must not fear men's words and harbor hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: When the Suzhou garrison withdrew, court scholars who favored peace all blamed Jun; Xiaozong again wrote to Jun, saying, "Today's frontier affairs rely on you above all—you must not fear men's words and grow hesitant.

sentences.zh: 前日舉事之初，朕與卿任之，今日亦須與卿終之。」

translations.literal: When we first undertook this venture, I shared responsibility with you; today I must see it through with you as well."
translations.idiomatic: When we first undertook this venture, I shared the responsibility with you; today I must see it through with you as well."

sentences.zh: 浚乃以魏勝守海州，陳敏守泗州，戚方守濠州，郭振守六合。

translations.literal: Jun then put Wei Sheng in charge of Haizhou, Chen Min of Sizhou, Qi Fang of Haozhou, and Guo Zhen of Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: Jun then put Wei Sheng in charge of Haizhou, Chen Min of Sizhou, Qi Fang of Haozhou, and Guo Zhen of Liuhe.

sentences.zh: 治高郵、巢縣兩城為大勢，修滁州關山以扼敵沖，聚水軍淮陰、馬軍壽春，大飭兩淮守備。

translations.literal: He built up Gaoyou and Chaoxian as major strongpoints, repaired the Guanshan pass at Chuzhou to block the enemy's thrust, concentrated naval forces at Huaiyin and cavalry at Shouchun, and greatly tightened defenses on the two Huai.
translations.idiomatic: He built up Gaoyou and Chaoxian as major strongpoints, repaired the Guanshan pass at Chuzhou to block the enemy's line of advance, concentrated naval forces at Huaiyin and cavalry at Shouchun, and greatly tightened defenses on the two Huai.

sentences.zh: 孝宗復召栻奏事，浚附奏云：「自古有為之君，腹心之臣相與協謀同志，以成治功。

translations.literal: Xiaozong again summoned Shi to report on affairs; Jun appended a memorial saying: "Since antiquity, when a ruler who acts decisively and a minister who is his heart's confidant join in counsel with one mind, they achieve good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong again summoned Shi to report on affairs; Jun appended a memorial saying, "Since antiquity, when a ruler who acts decisively and a minister who is his heart's confidant join in counsel with one mind, they achieve good governance.

sentences.zh: 今臣以孤蹤，動輒掣肘，陛下將安用之。」

translations.literal: Now I stand alone, and at every move I am checked—how does Your Majesty intend to use me?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I stand alone, and at every move I am checked—how does Your Majesty intend to use me?"

sentences.zh: 因乞骸骨。

translations.literal: He therefore requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore requested retirement.

sentences.zh: 孝宗覽奏，謂栻曰：「朕待魏公有加，不為浮議所惑。」

translations.literal: When Xiaozong read the memorial he said to Shi: "I treat the Duke of Wei with special favor and am not swayed by loose talk."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong read the memorial he said to Shi, "I treat the Duke of Wei with special favor and am not swayed by loose talk."

sentences.zh: 帝眷遇浚猶至，對近臣言，必曰魏公，未嘗斥其名。

translations.literal: The emperor's favor toward Jun remained as great as ever; speaking to close ministers he always said "the Duke of Wei" and never uttered his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's favor toward Jun remained as great as ever; speaking to close ministers he always said "the Duke of Wei" and never uttered his personal name.

sentences.zh: 每遣使來，必令視浚飲食多寡，肥瘠何如。

translations.literal: Whenever he sent an envoy, he always ordered him to observe how much Jun ate and drank and whether he was stout or thin.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he sent an envoy, he always ordered him to observe how much Jun ate and drank and whether he had grown stout or thin.

sentences.zh: 尋詔復浚都督之號。

translations.literal: Before long an edict restored Jun's title as overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict restored Jun's title as overall commander.

sentences.zh: 金帥僕散忠義貽書三省、樞密院，索四郡及歲幣，不然，以農隙治兵。

translations.literal: Jurchen commander Pusan Zhongyi sent a letter to the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs demanding four prefectures and the annual tribute; otherwise he would drill troops in the farming interval.
translations.idiomatic: Jurchen commander Pusan Zhongyi sent a letter to the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs demanding four prefectures and the annual tribute; otherwise he would drill troops during the farming interval.

sentences.zh: 浚言：「金強則來，弱則止，不在和與不和。」

translations.literal: Jun said: "When Jin is strong they come; when weak they stop—it does not depend on peace or no peace."
translations.idiomatic: Jun said, "When Jin is strong they come; when they are weak they stop—it does not depend on whether there is peace."

sentences.zh: 時湯思退為右相。

translations.literal: At that time Tang Situi was Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Tang Situi was Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 思退，秦檜黨也，急於求和，遂遣盧仲賢持書報金。

translations.literal: Situi was of Qin Hui's faction and eager for peace; he therefore dispatched Lu Zhongxian bearing a letter in reply to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Situi belonged to Qin Hui's faction and was eager for peace; he therefore dispatched Lu Zhongxian bearing a letter in reply to Jin.

sentences.zh: 浚言仲賢小人多妄，不可委信。

translations.literal: Jun said Zhongxian was a petty man prone to falsehood and could not be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Jun said Zhongxian was a petty man prone to falsehood and could not be entrusted with the mission.

sentences.zh: 已而仲賢果以許四郡辱命。

translations.literal: Before long Zhongxian indeed returned in disgrace after agreeing to the four prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Zhongxian indeed returned in disgrace after agreeing to cede the four prefectures.

sentences.zh: 朝廷復以王之望為通問使，龍大淵副之，浚爭不能得。

translations.literal: The court again appointed Wang Zhiwang as envoy for communications, with Long Dayuan as his deputy; Jun protested but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: The court again appointed Wang Zhiwang as envoy for communications, with Long Dayuan as his deputy; Jun protested but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召浚入見，復力陳和議之失。

translations.literal: Before long Jun was summoned for an audience and again argued forcefully against the peace talks.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Jun was summoned for an audience and again argued forcefully against the peace talks.

sentences.zh: 孝宗為止誓書，留之望、大淵待命，而令通書官胡昉、楊由義往，諭金以四郡不可割；

translations.literal: Xiaozong therefore halted the oath document, kept Wang Zhiwang and Long Dayuan awaiting orders, and sent communications officers Hu Fang and Yang Youyi instead to tell the Jurchens that the four prefectures could not be ceded;
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong therefore halted the oath document, kept Wang Zhiwang and Long Dayuan awaiting orders, and sent communications officers Hu Fang and Yang Youyi instead to tell the Jurchens that the four prefectures could not be ceded;

sentences.zh: 若金人必欲得四郡，當追還使人，罷和議。

translations.literal: if the Jurchens insisted on having the four prefectures, the envoys should be recalled and the peace talks broken off.
translations.idiomatic: if the Jurchens insisted on having the four prefectures, the envoys should be recalled and the peace talks broken off.

sentences.zh: 拜浚尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使，都督如故；

translations.literal: Jun was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Concurrent Grand Councillor, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, retaining his overall command;
translations.idiomatic: Jun was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Concurrent Grand Councillor, and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, retaining his overall command;

sentences.zh: 思退為左僕射。

translations.literal: Situi was made Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: Situi was made Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 胡昉等至宿，金人械系迫脅之，昉等不屈，更禮而歸之。

translations.literal: When Hu Fang and the others reached Suzhou, the Jurchens shackled and coerced them, but Hu and the others did not yield; they were treated with courtesy and sent back.
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Fang and the others reached Suzhou, the Jurchens shackled and coerced them, but Hu and the others did not yield; they were then treated with courtesy and sent back.

sentences.zh: 孝宗諭浚曰：「和議之不成，天也，自此事當歸一矣。」

translations.literal: Xiaozong told Jun: "That the peace talks failed was Heaven's doing; from this matter authority must be unified."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong told Jun, "That the peace talks failed was Heaven's doing; from this point authority must be unified."

sentences.zh: 二年，議進幸建康，詔之望等還。

translations.literal: In the second year, as an imperial visit to Jiankang was debated, Wang Zhiwang and the others were recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, as an imperial visit to Jiankang was debated, Wang Zhiwang and the others were recalled.

sentences.zh: 思退聞之大駭，陽為乞祠狀，而陰與其黨謀為陷浚計。

translations.literal: Situi was greatly alarmed on hearing this; he outwardly submitted a request for a temple post while secretly plotting with his faction to trap Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Situi was greatly alarmed on hearing this; he outwardly submitted a request for a temple post while secretly plotting with his faction to trap Jun.

sentences.zh: 俄詔浚行視江、淮。

translations.literal: Before long an edict ordered Jun to go inspect the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an edict ordered Jun to go inspect the Jiang and Huai.

sentences.zh: 時浚所招徠山東、淮北忠義之士，以實建康、鎮江兩軍，凡萬二千余人，萬弩營所招淮南壯士及江西群盜又萬余人，陳敏統之，以守泗州。

translations.literal: At that time loyalists Jun had recruited from Shandong and north of the Huai to fill out the Jiankang and Zhenjiang armies numbered more than twelve thousand in all; the Ten Thousand Crossbow Camp's recruits of Huainan stalwarts and Jiangxi bandits numbered more than ten thousand more, all under Chen Min's command to hold Sizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At that time loyalists Jun had recruited from Shandong and north of the Huai to fill out the Jiankang and Zhenjiang armies numbered more than twelve thousand in all; the Ten Thousand Crossbow Camp's recruits of Huainan stalwarts and Jiangxi bandits numbered more than ten thousand more, all under Chen Min's command to hold Sizhou.

sentences.zh: 凡要害之地，皆築城堡；

translations.literal: Every strategic point had fortified castles built;
translations.idiomatic: Every strategic point had fortified castles built;

sentences.zh: 其可因水為險者，皆積水為匱；

translations.literal: where terrain could be turned to advantage by water, reservoirs were piled up as barriers;
translations.idiomatic: where terrain could be turned to advantage by water, reservoirs were piled up as barriers;

sentences.zh: 增置江、淮戰艦，諸軍弓矢器械悉備。

translations.literal: Jiang and Huai warships were added, and bow, arrow, and weapon stocks in every army were fully supplied.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang and Huai warships were added, and every army was fully supplied with bows, arrows, and weapons.

sentences.zh: 時金人屯重兵于河南，為虛聲脅和，有刻日決戰之語。

translations.literal: At that time the Jurchens massed heavy forces in Henan, making empty threats to coerce peace, even speaking of a fixed day for decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Jurchens massed heavy forces in Henan, making empty threats to coerce peace, even speaking of a fixed day for decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 及聞浚來，亟徹兵歸。

translations.literal: When they heard Jun was coming, they hurriedly withdrew their troops.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Jun was coming, they hurriedly withdrew their troops.

sentences.zh: 淮北之來歸者日不絕，山東豪傑，悉願受節度。

translations.literal: Defectors from north of the Huai came in daily without cease; heroes of Shandong all wished to accept his command.
translations.idiomatic: Defectors from north of the Huai came in daily without cease; heroes of Shandong all wished to accept his command.

sentences.zh: 浚以蕭琦契丹望族，沈勇有謀，欲令盡領契丹降眾，且以檄諭契丹，約為應援，金人益懼。

translations.literal: Jun, because Xiao Qi was of Khitan noble lineage, deep courage and resourceful in planning, wished to have him lead all surrendered Khitans and also send a proclamation to the Khitans, arranging mutual support—the Jurchens grew still more afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, seeing that Xiao Qi was of Khitan noble lineage and was deep-courageous and resourceful, wished to have him lead all surrendered Khitans and also send a proclamation to the Khitans arranging mutual support—the Jurchens grew still more afraid.

sentences.zh: 思退乃令王之望盛毀守備，以為不可恃；

translations.literal: Situi then had Wang Zhiwang loudly disparage the defenses as unreliable;
translations.idiomatic: Situi then had Wang Zhiwang loudly disparage the defenses as unreliable;

sentences.zh: 令尹穡論罷督府參議官馮方；

translations.literal: he had Yin Ji memorialize to dismiss Feng Fang, a staff adviser at the command headquarters;
translations.idiomatic: he had Yin Ji memorialize to dismiss Feng Fang, a staff adviser at the command headquarters;

sentences.zh: 又論浚費國不貲，奏留張深守泗不受趙廓之代為拒命。

translations.literal: and again attacked Jun for wasting the state's resources beyond reckoning, memorializing that Zhang Shen be kept at Sizhou and refuse replacement by Zhao Kuo as defiance of orders.
translations.idiomatic: and again attacked Jun for wasting the state's resources beyond reckoning, memorializing that Zhang Shen be kept at Sizhou and refuse replacement by Zhao Kuo as defiance of orders.

sentences.zh: 浚亦請解督府，詔從其請。

translations.literal: Jun also requested to be relieved of the command headquarters; an edict granted his request.
translations.idiomatic: Jun also requested to be relieved of the command headquarters; an edict granted his request.

sentences.zh: 左司諫陳良翰、侍御史周操言浚忠勤，人望所屬，不當使去國。

translations.literal: Left Remonstrance Bureau Adviser Chen Lianghan and Attending Censor Zhou Cao said that Jun was loyal and diligent, the man to whom public expectation belonged, and that he ought not be made to leave the state.
translations.idiomatic: Left Remonstrance Bureau Adviser Chen Lianghan and Attending Censor Zhou Cao argued that Jun was loyal and diligent, the man in whom public trust was vested, and that he ought not be sent away from court.

sentences.zh: 浚留平江，凡八章乞致仕，除少師、保信軍節度、判福州。

translations.literal: Jun remained at Pingjiang; in eight memorials in all he begged to retire from office. He was appointed Junior Preceptor, given the Baoxin Army military commission, and entrusted with Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jun stayed at Pingjiang and submitted eight memorials in all requesting retirement. He was appointed Junior Preceptor, given the Baoxin Army military commission, and entrusted with Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 浚辭，改醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Jun declined, and was changed to Superintendent of Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Jun declined the appointment and was instead made Superintendent of Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遂決棄地求和之議。

translations.literal: The court thereupon decided the proposal to surrender territory and sue for peace.
translations.idiomatic: The court thereupon settled on a policy of surrendering territory in exchange for peace.

sentences.zh: 浚既去，猶上疏論尹穡奸邪，必誤國事，且勸上務學親賢。

translations.literal: After Jun had departed, he still submitted a memorial attacking Yin Ji as treacherous and wicked, saying he would surely ruin state affairs, and urging the emperor to devote himself to learning and keep worthy men near.
translations.idiomatic: Even after Jun had left office, he continued to memorialize the throne, denouncing Yin Ji as treacherous and wicked and warning that he would surely ruin state affairs, while urging the emperor to devote himself to learning and keep worthy men close at hand.

sentences.zh: 或勉浚勿復以時事為言，浚曰：「君臣之羲，無所逃於天地之間。

translations.literal: Some urged Jun not to speak again on current affairs. Jun said: "The righteousness between ruler and minister cannot be escaped anywhere between Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Jun not to speak out again on affairs of the day. Jun replied, "The bond of righteousness between ruler and minister admits no escape anywhere under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 吾荷兩朝厚恩，久屍重任，今雖去國，猶日望上心感悟，苟有所見，安忍弗言。

translations.literal: I have received deep grace from two reigns and long held a weighty post in name; though I have now left the state, I still daily hope the sovereign's heart may be moved to understanding. If I have any insight, how could I bear not to speak?
translations.idiomatic: I have received deep favor from two reigns and long borne a weighty charge; though I have now left court, I still look each day for the emperor's heart to be awakened. If I see something that must be said, how could I bear to hold my tongue?

sentences.zh: 上如欲復用浚，浚當即日就道，不敢以老病為辭。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty wishes to employ Jun again, Jun should set out that very day and dare not plead old age or illness.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty wishes to employ me again, I shall set out that very day and would not dare plead old age or illness.

sentences.zh: 如若等言，是誠何心哉！」

translations.literal: If I followed words such as yours, what would that truly reveal of my heart!"
translations.idiomatic: If I heeded advice such as yours, what sort of heart would that reveal!"

sentences.zh: 聞者聳然。

translations.literal: Those who heard were startled.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard him were deeply stirred.

sentences.zh: 行次餘幹，得疾，手書付二子曰：「吾嘗相國，不能恢復中原，雪祖宗之恥，即死，不當葬我先人墓左，葬我衡山下足矣。」

translations.literal: When he reached Yugan on the road he fell ill. He wrote by hand and entrusted it to his two sons, saying: "I once served as chief minister, yet could not recover the Central Plain or wipe away the shame of our forefathers. Even in death I ought not be buried to the left of my ancestors' tombs; bury me beneath Mount Heng and that will suffice."
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill at Yugan on the road, he wrote a letter by hand to his two sons: "I once served as chief minister, yet failed to recover the Central Plain or wipe away the shame of our forefathers. Even in death I do not deserve burial beside my ancestors' tombs; bury me beneath Mount Heng and that will be enough.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，孝宗震悼，輟視朝，贈太保，後加贈太師，諡忠獻。

translations.literal: When word of his death arrived, Xiaozong was shaken with grief, suspended court audiences, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian; later he was further enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhongxian, "Loyal and Dedicated."
translations.idiomatic: When news of his death reached the court, Xiaozong was stricken with grief, suspended the morning audience, and posthumously enfeoffed him as Grand Guardian; later he was further enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title Zhongxian, "Loyal and Dedicated."

sentences.zh: 浚幼有大志，及為熙河幕官，遍行邊壘，覽觀山川形勢，時時與舊戍守將握手飲酒，問祖宗以來守邊舊法，及軍陳方略之宜。

translations.literal: From youth Jun had great ambition. When he became a staff officer in Xihe, he traveled throughout the border fortresses, surveying mountains, rivers, and terrain. From time to time he clasped hands and drank with veteran frontier commanders, asking about border-defense methods since the founding forefathers and what was fitting in arraying armies and planning strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Jun had harbored great ambition from youth. As a staff officer in Xihe, he traveled every border fortress, studying mountains, rivers, and terrain. He would clasp hands and drink with veteran frontier commanders, asking them about border-defense methods since the founding of the dynasty and what was fitting in deploying armies and planning strategy.

sentences.zh: 故一旦起自疏遠，當樞筦之任，悉能通知邊事本末。

translations.literal: Therefore, once he rose from remote obscurity to bear the responsibility of the vital administration, he was able to know thoroughly the full course of frontier affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when he rose at last from remote obscurity to hold the reins of state, he understood frontier affairs from first cause to final consequence.

sentences.zh: 在京城中，親見二帝北行，皇族系虜，生民塗炭，誓不與敵俱存，故終身不主和議。

translations.literal: In the capital he had personally seen the two emperors taken north, the imperial clan bound by the enemy, and the people plunged into fire and water. He swore not to exist together with the foe, and therefore never advocated peace talks throughout his life.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he had witnessed the two emperors carried north, the imperial clan held captive, and the people plunged into misery. He swore never to coexist with the enemy, and for the rest of his life he never advocated peace.

sentences.zh: 每論定都大計，以為東南形勢，莫如建康，人主居之，可以北望中原，常懷憤惕。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed the great plan of fixing the capital, he held that among the strategic positions of the southeast none matched Jiankang: if the sovereign dwelt there, he could look north toward the Central Plain and constantly cherish indignation and vigilance.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he discussed where the capital should be fixed, he argued that among the strategic positions of the southeast none matched Jiankang: if the sovereign resided there, he could look north toward the Central Plain and keep alive both indignation and vigilance.

sentences.zh: 至如錢塘，僻在一隅，易於安肆，不足以號召北方。

translations.literal: As for Qiantang, tucked away in a corner, it easily lulls one into ease and indulgence and is insufficient to summon the north.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantang, by contrast, lay tucked away in a corner, inviting ease and complacency, and could not rally the north.

sentences.zh: 與趙鼎共政，多所引擢，從臣朝列，皆一時之望，人號「小元祐」。

translations.literal: Sharing government with Zhao Ding, he promoted many men; attendant ministers and court officials were all luminaries of the age, and people called it the "Lesser Yuanyou."
translations.idiomatic: While sharing power with Zhao Ding, he promoted many men of talent; the attendant ministers and court officials were all luminaries of the age, and people called their administration the "Lesser Yuanyou."

sentences.zh: 所薦虞允文、汪應辰、王十朋、劉珙等為名臣；

translations.literal: Those he recommended—Yu Yunwen, Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Liu Gong, and others—became renowned ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Those he recommended—Yu Yunwen, Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Liu Gong, and others—became renowned ministers;

sentences.zh: 拔吳玠、吳璘於行間，謂韓世忠忠勇，可倚以大事，一見劉錡奇之，付以事任，卒皆為名將，有成功，一時稱浚為知人。

translations.literal: He plucked Wu Jie and Wu Lin from the ranks; he said Han Shizhong was loyal and brave and could be relied on for great affairs; at first sight of Liu Qi he regarded him as extraordinary and entrusted him with responsibility. In the end all became famous generals with achievements, and for a time people praised Jun as knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: He plucked Wu Jie and Wu Lin from the ranks; he declared Han Shizhong loyal and brave and fit to be relied on for great undertakings; at first sight of Liu Qi he recognized his exceptional talent and entrusted him with command. In the end they all became famous generals who won success, and for a time people praised Jun as a man who truly knew talent.

sentences.zh: 浚事母以孝稱，學邃于《易》，有《易解》及《雜說》十卷，《書》、《詩》、《禮》、《春秋》、《中庸》亦各有解，文集十卷，奏議二十卷。

translations.literal: Jun was famed for filial service to his mother. He was deeply learned in the Book of Changes and had Commentaries on the Changes and Miscellaneous Discourses in ten juan; he also wrote commentaries on the Documents, Odes, Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Doctrine of the Mean, a collected writings in ten juan, and memorials and deliberations in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was renowned for filial devotion to his mother. Deeply learned in the Book of Changes, he wrote Commentaries on the Changes and Miscellaneous Discourses in ten juan, along with commentaries on the Documents, Odes, Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, and Doctrine of the Mean; his collected writings ran to ten juan, and his memorials and deliberations to twenty.

sentences.zh: 子二人、栻、枃。

translations.literal: He had two sons: Shi and Shi.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Shi and Shi.

sentences.zh: 栻自有傳。

translations.literal: Shi has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Shi has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 子 枃

translations.literal: Son: Shi
translations.idiomatic: Son: Shi

sentences.zh: 枃字定叟，以父恩授承奉郎，曆廣西經略司機宜、通判嚴州。

translations.literal: Shi, courtesy name Dingsou, received appointment as Gentleman for Meritorious Service through his father's grace. He successively served as staff officer in the Guangxi Pacification Commission and as vice prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shi, courtesy name Dingsou, received appointment as Gentleman for Meritorious Service through his father's patronage. He served successively as staff officer on the Guangxi Pacification Commission and as vice prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 方年少，已有能稱，浙西使者薦所部吏而不及枃，孝宗特令再薦。

translations.literal: Though still young, he already had a reputation for ability. When the Zhexi commissioner recommended officials under his jurisdiction but did not include Shi, Xiaozong specially ordered a second round of recommendations.
translations.idiomatic: Though still young, he already enjoyed a reputation for ability. When the Zhexi commissioner recommended officials under his jurisdiction but omitted Shi, Xiaozong specially ordered that he be recommended again.

sentences.zh: 召對，差知袁州，戢豪強，弭盜賊。

translations.literal: Summoned for audience, he was dispatched to serve as prefect of Yuan Prefecture, where he restrained powerful bullies and quelled bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned for audience, he was appointed prefect of Yuan Prefecture, where he restrained local bullies and suppressed banditry.

sentences.zh: 尉獲盜上之州，枃察知其枉，縱去，莫不怪之，未幾，果獲真盜。

translations.literal: When the district captain seized a thief and sent him up to the prefecture, Shi perceived that the man had been wronged, released him, and everyone thought it strange. Before long the real thief was indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: When the district captain arrested a thief and sent him to the prefecture, Shi saw that the man had been wrongfully accused, released him, and astonished everyone. Before long the real thief was captured.

sentences.zh: 改知衢州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 兄栻喪，無壯子，請祠以營葬事，主管玉局觀，遷湖北提舉常平。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Shi died leaving no adult son, he requested a sinecure to arrange the burial and was made superintendent of Jade Bureau Abbey; he was then transferred to Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Shi died without leaving an adult son, he requested a sinecure to arrange the burial and was made superintendent of Jade Bureau Abbey; he was then transferred to Intendant of Ever-Normal Granaries in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 奏事，帝大喜，諭輔臣曰：「張浚有子如此。」

translations.literal: When he reported on affairs, the emperor was greatly pleased and instructed the chief ministers, saying: "Zhang Jun has a son like this."
translations.idiomatic: When he reported on affairs, the emperor was greatly pleased and told the chief ministers, "Zhang Jun has a son like this."

sentences.zh: 改浙西，督理荒政，蘇、湖二州皆闕守，命兼攝焉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Zhexi to supervise famine relief. Both Su and Hu prefectures lacked prefects, and he was ordered to hold those posts concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Zhexi to supervise famine relief. Both Su and Hu prefectures lacked prefects, and he was ordered to hold those posts concurrently.

sentences.zh: 有執政姻黨閉糶，枃首治之，帝獎其不畏強禦，遷兩浙轉運判官。

translations.literal: When a kinsman of a chief minister hoarded grain and refused to sell, Shi took the lead in punishing him. The emperor praised him for not fearing the powerful and transferred him to Vice Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhes.
translations.idiomatic: When a kinsman of a chief minister hoarded grain and refused to sell it, Shi took the lead in prosecuting him. The emperor praised him for fearlessness in the face of power and transferred him to Vice Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhes.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以直徽猷閣升副使，改知臨安府。

translations.literal: Before long, through his appointment as Direct Attendant of the Hall of Splendid Learning he was promoted to Vice Commissioner and transferred to serve as prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, on the strength of his appointment as Direct Attendant of the Hall of Splendid Learning, he was promoted to Vice Commissioner and appointed prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 奏除逋欠四萬緡，米八百斛，進直龍圖閣。

translations.literal: He memorialized to remit four myriad strings of overdue payments and eight hundred hu of grain, and was advanced to Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to remit forty thousand strings of overdue payments and eight hundred hu of grain, and was promoted to Direct Attendant of the Dragon Diagram Hall.

sentences.zh: 都城浩穰，奸盜聚慝，枃畫分地以警捕，夜戶不閉。

translations.literal: The capital was vast and crowded; villains and thieves gathered in wickedness. Shi mapped out districts for patrol and arrest, and at night households did not close their doors.
translations.idiomatic: The capital was vast and crowded, and villains and thieves flourished. Shi divided the city into districts for patrol and arrest, until at night people no longer barred their doors.

sentences.zh: 張師尹納女掖庭供給使，恃以恣橫，枃因事痛繩之，徙其家信州，其類帖伏。

translations.literal: Zhang Shiyin presented a daughter to serve as a supply attendant in the inner quarters and relied on this to act wantonly. Shi seized an occasion to punish him severely, moved his household to Xin Prefecture, and his kind submitted in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Shiyin had presented a daughter to serve as a supply attendant in the inner quarters and relied on that connection to act with impunity. Shi seized an opportunity to punish him severely, exiled his household to Xin Prefecture, and his ilk submitted in fear.

sentences.zh: 南郊禮成，賜五品服，權兵部侍郎，仍知臨安，加賜三品服。

translations.literal: When the southern suburban rites were completed, he was granted fifth-rank robes, made Acting Vice Minister of War while still serving as prefect of Lin'an, and further granted third-rank robes.
translations.idiomatic: When the southern suburban rites were completed, he was granted fifth-rank robes, appointed Acting Vice Minister of War while continuing as prefect of Lin'an, and further granted third-rank robes.

sentences.zh: 修三閘，復六井。

translations.literal: He repaired three sluice gates and restored six wells.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired three sluice gates and restored six wells.

sentences.zh: 府治火，延及民居，上疏自劾，詔削二秩。

translations.literal: Fire broke out in the prefectural offices and spread to private dwellings. He submitted a memorial impeaching himself, and an edict stripped him of two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When fire broke out in the prefectural offices and spread to private dwellings, he memorialized to impeach himself, and an edict stripped him of two ranks.

sentences.zh: 枃再疏乞罷，移知鎮江。

translations.literal: Shi again memorialized begging to be dismissed and was transferred to serve as prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi memorialized again requesting dismissal and was transferred to serve as prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 尋改明州，辭，仍知鎮江。

translations.literal: Soon he was changed to Ming Prefecture; he declined, and remained prefect of Zhenjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was reassigned to Ming Prefecture; he declined, and remained prefect of Zhenjiang.

sentences.zh: 召為戶部侍郎，面對言事，迕時相意。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Vice Minister of Revenue, spoke on affairs in audience, and ran counter to the chief councillor's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Vice Minister of Revenue, spoke frankly on affairs in audience, and ran counter to the chief councillor's wishes.

sentences.zh: 高宗崩，以集英殿修撰知紹興府，董山陵事。

translations.literal: When Gaozong died, he was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Shaoxing, and directed the imperial tomb works.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong died, he was made Compiler at the Hall for Assembling Excellence and prefect of Shaoxing, charged with overseeing the imperial tomb works.

sentences.zh: 召還，為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was recalled and made Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 光宗即位，權刑部侍郎，復兼知臨安府。

translations.literal: When Guangzong ascended the throne, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Justice and again given concurrent appointment as prefect of Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzong ascended the throne, he was made Acting Vice Minister of Justice and again given concurrent appointment as prefect of Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 紹熙元年，為刑部侍郎，仍為府尹。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shaoxi he became Vice Minister of Justice while still serving as prefect of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Shaoxi he became Vice Minister of Justice while continuing to serve as prefect of the capital.

sentences.zh: 內侍毛伯益冒西湖茭地為亭，外戚有殺其僕者，獄具，夤緣宣諭求免，枃皆執奏論如律。

translations.literal: Palace attendant Mao Boyi encroached on West Lake reed lands to build a pavilion. A consort kinsman had killed his servant; when the case was complete, he used connections to seek exemption through an imperial message. In every instance Shi firmly memorialized that the law should be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant Mao Boyi encroached on West Lake reed lands to build a pavilion. A consort kinsman had killed his servant; when the case was complete, he used connections to seek exemption through an imperial message. In every instance Shi firmly memorialized that the law must be applied.

sentences.zh: 孝宗觀湖，枃以彈壓伏謁道左，孝宗止輦問勞，賜以酒炙。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong toured the lake, Shi, having kept order, prostrated himself to greet him on the left of the road. Xiaozong halted the carriage to inquire after him and bestowed wine and roasted meat.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong toured the lake, Shi, having kept order along the route, prostrated himself to greet him by the roadside. Xiaozong halted the carriage to inquire after him and bestowed wine and roasted meat.

sentences.zh: 京西謀帥，進煥章閣學士、知襄陽府，賜金二百兩，別賜金百兩，白金倍之。

translations.literal: As the court sought a commander for Jingxi, he was advanced to Academician of the Hall of Resplendent Insignia and made prefect of Xiangyang. He was granted two hundred liang of gold, separately granted one hundred liang of gold, and twice that amount in silver.
translations.idiomatic: As the court sought a commander for Jingxi, he was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Resplendent Insignia and appointed prefect of Xiangyang. He was granted two hundred liang of gold, separately granted one hundred liang more, and twice that amount in silver.

sentences.zh: 未幾，進徽猷閣學士、知建康府，繼復命還襄陽。

translations.literal: Before long he was advanced to Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning and made prefect of Jiankang; soon afterward he was again ordered back to Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Splendid Learning and appointed prefect of Jiankang; soon afterward he was ordered back to Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 甯宗嗣位，歸正人陳應祥、忠義人黨琪等謀襲均州，副都統馮湛間道疾馳以聞。

translations.literal: When Ningzong succeeded to the throne, returned-allegiance men Chen Yingxiang, loyalty-and-righteousness men Dang Qi, and others plotted a surprise attack on Jun Prefecture. Vice Commander-in-Chief Feng Zhan raced by a hidden route to report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Ningzong succeeded to the throne, returned-allegiance men Chen Yingxiang, loyalty-and-righteousness men Dang Qi, and others plotted a surprise attack on Jun Prefecture. Vice Commander-in-Chief Feng Zhan raced by a hidden route to report it.

sentences.zh: 枃不為動，徐部分掩捕，獄成，斬其為首者二人，盡釋黨與，反側以安。

translations.literal: Shi was not shaken. Deliberately he divided his forces for a concealed arrest; when the case was complete he executed the two ringleaders, released all their associates, and the restless were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was not shaken. Calmly he divided his forces for a concealed arrest; when the case was complete he executed the two ringleaders, released all their associates, and the region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 升寶文閣學士、知平江府，未行，改知建康府。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Precious Classics and made prefect of Pingjiang; before he set out, he was changed to prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Precious Classics and appointed prefect of Pingjiang; before he departed, he was reassigned to prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 升龍圖閣學士、知隆興府兼江西安撫使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, made prefect of Longxing, and given concurrent appointment as Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall, appointed prefect of Longxing, and given concurrent appointment as Jiangxi Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奉新縣舊有營田，募民耕之，畝賦米鬥五升，錢六十，其後議臣請鬻之。

translations.literal: Fengxin County formerly had military colony fields; civilians were recruited to cultivate them, with a levy of five sheng of grain per mu and sixty cash. Later deliberating officials requested that they be sold off.
translations.idiomatic: Fengxin County had long maintained military colony fields worked by recruited civilians, with a levy of five sheng of grain per mu and sixty cash. Later deliberating officials requested that the land be sold off.

sentences.zh: 始，征兩稅和買，且加折變，民重為困，枃悉奏蠲之。

translations.literal: At first the two taxes and state purchases were levied, with conversion surcharges added besides, and the people were heavily burdened. Shi memorialized to remit all of these.
translations.idiomatic: At first the two taxes and state purchases were levied, with conversion surcharges added on top, and the people were heavily burdened. Shi memorialized to remit all of these levies.

sentences.zh: 進端明殿學士，復知建康府。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and again made prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Academician of the Hall of Manifest Brightness and again appointed prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 以疾乞祠，卒。

translations.literal: He begged a sinecure on grounds of illness and died.
translations.idiomatic: He requested a sinecure on grounds of illness and died.

sentences.zh: 枃天分高爽，吏材敏給，遇事不凝滯，多隨宜變通，所至以治辨稱。

translations.literal: Shi was by nature lofty and clear-minded, quick and capable in administrative talent. In handling affairs he did not grow rigid, but adapted flexibly as circumstances required, and wherever he went he was praised for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shi was by nature lofty and clear-minded, quick and capable in administration. He did not grow rigid when handling affairs, but adapted flexibly as circumstances required, and wherever he served he was praised for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 再渡以來，論尹京者，以枃為首。

translations.literal: Since the second crossing south, among those who have governed the capital, Shi is ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: Since the court's second crossing south, among those who have governed the capital, Shi ranks first.

sentences.zh: 子忠純、忠恕，自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons Zhongchun and Zhongshu have their own biographies.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zhongchun and Zhongshu have their own biographies.

sentences.zh: 論曰：儒者之於國家，能養其正直之氣，則足以正君心，一眾志，攘凶逆，處憂患，蓋無往而不自得焉。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: For the state, when Confucian scholars can nourish their upright qi, they are sufficient to rectify the ruler's heart, unify the will of the multitude, repel fierce rebels, and meet with calamity—indeed there is nowhere they cannot find their proper ease.
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal says: In service to the state, when Confucian scholars can nourish their upright spirit, they are sufficient to rectify the ruler's heart, unify the people's will, repel fierce rebels, and meet calamity with composure—there is scarcely a situation in which they cannot find their proper footing.

sentences.zh: 若張浚者，可謂善養其氣者矣。

translations.literal: A man such as Zhang Jun may be called one who knew well how to nourish his qi.
translations.idiomatic: A man such as Zhang Jun may truly be called one who knew how to nourish his spirit.

sentences.zh: 觀其初逃張邦昌之議，平苗、劉之亂，其才識固有非偷懦之所敢望。

translations.literal: Consider how at the outset he fled the deliberations over Zhang Bangchang and quelled the Miao and Liu rebellion: his talent and insight were indeed not what the timid and craven would dare aspire to.
translations.idiomatic: Consider how at the outset he fled the deliberations over Zhang Bangchang and quelled the Miao and Liu rebellion: his talent and insight were indeed beyond what the timid and craven could aspire to.

sentences.zh: 及其攘卻勍敵，招降劇盜，能使將帥用命，所向如志。

translations.literal: When he repelled fierce enemies and summoned fierce bandits to surrender, he could make generals and commanders obey orders, and wherever he turned his aim matched his will.
translations.idiomatic: When he repelled fierce enemies and induced fierce bandits to surrender, he could make generals and commanders obey orders, and wherever he turned his aim matched his will.

sentences.zh: 遠人伺其用舍為進退，天下占其出處為安危，豈非卓然所謂人豪者歟！

translations.literal: Men afar watched whether he was employed or dismissed to gauge advance or retreat; all under Heaven read his emergence or withdrawal as signs of safety or peril—is this not manifestly what is called a towering hero!
translations.idiomatic: Men afar watched whether he was employed or dismissed to gauge advance or retreat; all under Heaven read his emergence or withdrawal as signs of safety or peril—is this not manifestly what is meant by a towering hero!

sentences.zh: 群言沸騰，屢奮屢躓，而辭氣慨然。

translations.literal: When talk seethed all around, though he rose repeatedly and stumbled repeatedly, his words and bearing remained impassioned.
translations.idiomatic: Though talk seethed all around and he rose repeatedly only to stumble again, his words and bearing remained impassioned.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「上如欲復用浚，當即日就道，不敢以老病辭。」

translations.literal: He once said: "If Your Majesty wishes to employ Jun again, Jun should set out that very day and dare not plead old age or illness."
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "If Your Majesty wishes to employ me again, I shall set out that very day and would not dare plead old age or illness."

sentences.zh: 其言如是，則其愛君憂國之心，為何如哉！

translations.literal: When his words were such as this, what then of his heart that loved the ruler and grieved for the state!
translations.idiomatic: When his words were such as these, what more need be said of the heart that loved his ruler and grieved for his state!

sentences.zh: 時論以浚之忠大類漢諸葛亮，然亮能使魏延、楊儀終其身不為異同，浚以吳玠故遂殺曲端，亮能容法孝直，浚不能容李綱、趙鼎而又詆之，茲所以為不及歟！

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held that Jun's loyalty greatly resembled that of Zhuge Liang of Han; yet Liang could keep Wei Yan and Yang Yi from becoming divided throughout their lives, while Jun, because of Wu Jie, went so far as to execute Qu Duan. Liang could tolerate Fa Xiaozhi, while Jun could not tolerate Li Gang and Zhao Ding and moreover slandered them—is this not why he fell short!
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary opinion held that Jun's loyalty greatly resembled that of Zhuge Liang of Han; yet Liang could keep Wei Yan and Yang Yi from turning against each other throughout their lives, while Jun, because of Wu Jie, went so far as to execute Qu Duan. Liang could tolerate Fa Xiaozhi, while Jun could not tolerate Li Gang and Zhao Ding and moreover slandered them—is this not why he fell short!

sentences.zh: 至於富平之潰師，淮西之兵變，則成敗利鈍，雖亮不能逆睹也。

translations.literal: As for the routed army at Fuping and the mutiny in Huai West, success and failure, advantage and setback—even Liang could not foresee them in advance.
translations.idiomatic: As for the routed army at Fuping and the mutiny in Huai West, success and failure, advantage and setback—even Liang could not have foreseen them in advance.
